findings.claim: The criterion perf-budget gate DOES run per-PR (`just eval` calls `just perf-budget`, and ci.yml runs `just eval`), on a shared ubuntu-latest runner, measuring wall-clock. Under those conditions the ~20x ceilings are the CORRECT engineering call, not laziness — the file says so explicitly ("the gate catches order-of-magnitude regressions, not 5% drift") and every entry carries its measured value, date and conditions. Tightening those ceilings on wall-clock CI would buy flakiness, not sensitivity.
findings.source: MEASURED: justfile:28-30 (`eval:` -> `node evals/run.mjs` then `just perf-budget`), justfile:45-50 (`perf-budget` -> `cargo bench -p game-core --bench hot_paths`), .github/workflows/ci.yml `- run: just eval`; game-core/benches/budgets.rs:12-14 and the per-entry AM11 provenance block :24-33
findings.caveat: NOT_APPLICABLE as a defect. The 20x ceiling is not the bug; expecting a wall-clock gate to detect small regressions would be.

findings.claim: The only way to get a tight, non-flaky perf ceiling in CI is to stop measuring time. iai-callgrind uses Valgrind/Callgrind instruction counts — "extremely accurate and consistent measurements ... perfectly suited to run in environments like a CI", detecting regressions "even in noisy environments with a precision that is impossible to achieve with wall-clock time based benchmarks", one run per benchmark instead of many. VERSION CAVEAT: the crate `iai-callgrind` is frozen at 0.16.1 (last published 2025-07-30); the project was renamed and now publishes as `gungraun` 0.19.4 (2026-07-10). SpacetimeDB's own vendor (clockworklabs) maintains a fork.
findings.source: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/iai-callgrind (max_version 0.16.1, updated 2025-07-30); https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/gungraun (max_version 0.19.4, updated 2026-07-10); https://github.com/iai-callgrind/iai-callgrind (redirects to gungraun/gungraun); https://bencher.dev/rust/iai-callgrind/
findings.caveat: Costs: a valgrind apt install in CI, a second bench harness to maintain, a rename migration already in flight, and it measures instructions not nanoseconds so the existing ns budgets do not port. Given the 7 hot paths measure 1.87-134.5 ns and nothing in the post-mortem attributes an escaped defect to perf, this is a LATER item, not a now item.

findings.claim: There is no credible off-the-shelf "delete budget" or test-consolidation gate. The academic prior art is test-suite reduction driven by mutation attribution: retain only tests that kill at least one mutant no other test kills; "tests that kill no mutant are identified as the most fragile test methods"; and coverage-based redundancy detection is explicitly known to produce "a large number of false-positive errors, with test cases being identified as redundant while they are really not". No mainstream tool implements this for Rust or for a bespoke .eval.mjs corpus, and cargo-mutants has no per-test attribution output.
findings.source: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-28872-2_29 (Reduction of Test Suites Using Mutation); https://hindawi.com/journals/ase/2010/932686 (tester-assisted redundancy detection, false-positive warning); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.12085 (Characterizing High-Quality Test Methods); MEASURED: `cargo mutants --help` has no per-test attribution or reduction output
findings.caveat: Do not build a line-count budget on the test corpus. It is gameable in both directions and the literature says coverage-based redundancy detection is unreliable. The only defensible automatic signal — mutation attribution — is not available from the installed tool.

research.recommendation:
DO, in this order — each is small, each replaces agent-written scanner code with off-the-shelf tooling, and every one of them costs CI minutes rather than Claude plan credits (an important asymmetry under the operator's secondary priority: CI compute is NOT the weekly allowance).

1. WIRE THE VALIDATOR THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Add `node ops/observability/validate.mjs` to a justfile recipe and call it from a nightly job. Zero new code. It already runs `docker compose config --quiet`, promtool check config/rules, alloy fmt, loki -verify-config, tempo -config.verify and caddy validate through the pinned images, and already distinguishes `skipped` from `pass`. Today it has zero mechanical callers and ARCHITECTURE.md:1405 cites a one-time hand-run as if it were a gate. This is the highest value-per-credit item in the whole research brief.

2. ADD `healthcheck:` TO ALL 8 SERVICES, THEN A BOOT SMOKE JOB. Nightly: `docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 180` followed by an assertion that every service is `State=running` with `RestartCount==0`, then `down -v`. Zero healthchecks exist today and every service carries `restart: unless-stopped`, which is exactly why 4 of 8 crash-loopers merged CLEAN. This is the check that catches the tempo bogus-flag class — `docker compose config` cannot, because the flag is syntactically valid YAML. Then DELETE the tempo `-server.http-listen-address` line and fix `checkListenAddrsLoopback` to read tempo/tempo-config.yml, per the prescription already written in evals/observability-stack-config.eval.mjs:153-157.

3. ADD A PER-PR `--in-diff` MUTATION LEG AND DELETE mr-audit's gating_test_audit. New ci.yml job (or a `mutation-diff` job in a new workflow), path-filtered per the book's example: `git diff origin/${{ github.base_ref }}... > /tmp/pr.diff` then `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff /tmp/pr.diff --annotations github -p monster-realm-module -p game-core --test-tool nextest`, zero survivors tolerated IN THE DIFF, `mutants.out` uploaded with `if: always()`. This is the mechanically correct replacement for gating_test_audit's lexical diff-shape check (0 true positives / 446 rows): instead of guessing whether a diff "looks tested", it deletes the code you just wrote and demands a test notice. It is also the only cheap gate that catches "a security guard removable without any test failing" AT THE MOMENT THE GUARD IS WRITTEN. Retire gating_test_audit in the same change — do not run both.

4. CONVERT `mutate-server` FROM AN ABSOLUTE CAP TO A RATE RATCHET + A NAMED-DEBT LIST. Read `mutants.out/outcomes.json` (not `grep -c missed.txt`) to get missed/(missed+caught) and gate on survival RATE with an explicit tolerance band — the absolute cap of 324 is calibrated finer than the tool's own +/-1 local-vs-hosted reproducibility (ADR-0183 D1/D2, 323 vs 324 on a semantically identical tree). Then GENERALISE the repo's own best gate: `evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs`'s `KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7` pattern — a cap constant that must equal the entry count, entries validated to STILL be failing (so fixing one REDs the gate demanding the entry be deleted), each with an owner slice and a MEASURED reason. That is Betterer's two-way `betterer ci` semantic, hand-rolled and already working here. Apply it to the 11 named killable server-module survivors from ADR-0183 instead of a scalar. Add `if: failure()` notification wiring to nightly.yml, which currently has none.

5. MOVE GUARDS INTO game-core SEAMS AS THE STANDING RULE FOR NEW WORK. `authorize_respond`/`authorize_confirm`/`check_headroom` in game-core/src/trading/rules.rs are the proven template: pure function, real behavioural tests, and automatically covered by the zero-tolerance `mutate-core` gate. Once a guard lives there, the source-scan degrades to "does the reducer still call the seam" — a one-line needle instead of a whole-file semantic parse. This is the only durable path off the 94k-line eval scanner corpus, and it is a per-slice habit, not a migration project.

6. CLOSE 14r-c-2 (the 6 blind security evals) using the tracking gate that already enumerates them. That gate is red-by-design with a shrinking cap. It is the correct mechanism; it just needs the slice.

DO NOT:
- Do NOT introduce proptest or fast-check "adoption" work. Both are already in use (34 proptest! sites / 28 files; 113 fc.assert / ~40 files). Property testing is not the gap. It also cannot reach a reducer guard, so it does not solve the escaped-defect class.
- Do NOT bump fast-check 3->4 or chase proptest currency. No escaped defect traces to either.
- Do NOT build a reducer-executing harness. There is no `spacetimedb-testing` crate; bindings-sys is the wasm host ABI and reducer bodies cannot execute natively. The publish-and-call path already exists (nightly smoke-republish, e2e job). Extend that if you need executing coverage; do not invent a harness.
- Do NOT replace the nightly full mutation run with `--in-diff`. The book is explicit: "not a substitute for a full test run", and the diff is matched only against code under test, never test code — a PR that guts tests generates zero mutants and reads green. Keep both legs.
- Do NOT use `--iterate` in CI. The docs recommend it for local iteration only; it assumes new changes cannot reduce coverage.
- Do NOT shard yet. ADR-0050:202-206 records 43 min hosted at 499 mutants and the extrapolation to 753 stays inside the nightly window. Add `--in-place` (the book's one explicit CI recommendation, currently unused) before adding a matrix.
- Do NOT tighten the criterion perf ceilings. 20x is the honest number for wall-clock benchmarking on a shared runner and the file documents why. If a tight ceiling ever becomes necessary, the answer is instruction counting (gungraun 0.19.4, formerly iai-callgrind 0.16.1), not a smaller multiplier.
- Do NOT add a line-count or "delete budget" gate on the test corpus. There is no credible prior art; coverage-based redundancy detection is documented as false-positive-prone; and the only defensible signal (per-test mutation attribution) is not emitted by cargo-mutants. The real simplification pressure comes free from items 1-3: every scanner that an off-the-shelf tool supersedes becomes deletable with a named replacement.
- Do NOT add more `#[mutants::skip]` or `exclude_re` entries as a way to move the number. The existing `.cargo/mutants.toml` is exemplary (3 line-pinned entries, each with a proof of equivalence, one already retired when it stopped being equivalent). Keep that bar.
unknowns: Actual hosted wall-clock for the current 753-mutant server-module run. ADR-0183's hosted row leaves the duration blank; the only recorded hosted figure is 43 min at 499 mutants (ADR-0050:205). The ~155 min in the brief is not in the corpus. A single `workflow_dispatch` of the nightly with timing captured would settle it, and it decides whether sharding is needed.

Cost of a per-PR `--in-diff` leg in CI minutes. It depends on baseline build time for `monster-realm-module` plus mutants-per-diff, neither measured. Estimate from one dry run on a representative merged slice diff before wiring it as a blocking gate.
Whether `cargo mutants --in-place` is safe alongside the existing `Swatinem/rust-cache` prefix keys, or whether it perturbs the cached target dir in a way that costs more than the copy it saves.

Exact field names in `mutants.out/outcomes.json`. The book confirms the file exists and holds "summary counts of each outcome" but does not document the schema. Read one real file (`cargo mutants --list` then a short scoped run) before writing a rate parser against it.
Whether GitHub Actions minutes are billed on this repo (private vs public). If billed, items 2 and 3 have a real dollar cost that must be weighed even though it is not plan credits.
Whether loki 3.7.6 and tempo 2.10.7 expose stable readiness endpoints at the loopback ports this compose file binds — needed to write correct `healthcheck:` blocks rather than guessed ones.

Whether any of the 11 killable server-module survivors named in ADR-0183 are reducer-body mutants (unreachable without a harness) versus game-core-extractable. That split determines whether the ratchet-to-313 slice is small or blocked.

research.topic: Testing SpacetimeDB 2.6.0 reducers: official support, real-world practice, and the cheapest correct harness for monster-realm

findings.claim: There is NO official in-process / in-crate reducer test harness for SpacetimeDB at any version, including 2.6.0. ReducerContext is #[non_exhaustive] with no new, no Default, and no mock/test constructor — it is structurally impossible to construct one from an external crate. There is no test ReducerContext, no embedded/in-memory TestDb type, and no `spacetime test` CLI command. Option (c) as literally specified (a fake ReducerContext) is not merely hard, it is impossible without removing ReducerContext from reducer bodies entirely.
findings.source: https://docs.rs/spacetimedb/1.12.0/spacetimedb/struct.ReducerContext.html (public fields sender/timestamp/connection_id/db; methods random/rng/sender_auth/identity/as_read_only/new_uuid_v4/new_uuid_v7; no constructor). Verified locally: `spacetime --help` on /home/mdrewt/.local/share/spacetime/bin/2.6.0/spacetimedb-cli lists 20 subcommands, none named `test`.

findings.claim: Clockwork Labs has two OPEN, unanswered issues confirming the gap is upstream, not local. #2833 'testing reducers' (open, filed 2025-06-05) asks for precisely what this project needs — isolated DB per test, pre-population, calling reducers as a client, peeking at the DB as the server, multiple identities, test source in the module tree — with no maintainer response or proposed API. #2788 'Add spacetime test command' (open, filed 2025-05-24, no assignee, no label, no milestone) documents that plain `cargo test` on a module crate can fail to link (MSVC LNK1120: 14 unresolved externals on datastore_insert_bsatn, console_log, table_id_from_name). No roadmap commitment on either.
findings.source: https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/issues/2833 ; https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/issues/2788
findings.caveat: The #2788 link error is symbol-resolution-eager MSVC. This repo's `cargo nextest run --workspace` (justfile:24-25) links fine on Linux because no in-crate test ever REFERENCES a host-ABI symbol. The moment a test touches ctx.db it would pull in the #[link(wasm_import_module="spacetime_10.x")] externs in spacetimedb-bindings-sys-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:21,594,623,649,775. So the in-crate ceiling is real, and it is exactly where the corpus stopped.

findings.claim: SpacetimeDB's OWN answer to 'how do you test a module' is: publish it to a real running instance and drive it over the wire. Their TESTING.md describes four suites and NONE of them execute a reducer in-process: (1) crates/testing/src/sdk.rs builds and freshly publishes a module to a short-lived empty database, runs `spacetime generate`, compiles a client project, runs it as a subprocess, exit code = pass/fail; (2) crates/schema/tests/ensure_same_schema.rs compares extracted schemas across languages; (3) crates/smoketests/ drives the CLI end-to-end; (4) crates/testing/tests/standalone_integration_test.rs publishes modules/module-test{,-cs,-ts,-cpp}, invokes their reducers, and inspects the LOGS to verify behaviour. Publishing to a live instance and asserting on server-observable state is the officially sanctioned pattern — not a workaround.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/master/TESTING.md ; https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/blob/master/modules/module-test/README.md

findings.claim: MEASURED, END TO END, ON THIS MACHINE, TODAY: a reducer-executing behavioural harness for this exact module is buildable from tools already installed and already used in CI. I started an ephemeral in-memory instance (`spacetime start --in-memory --listen-addr 127.0.0.1:3999`) — READY IN 2 SECONDS. I published the repo's already-built wasm via `publish --bin-path <wasm> --delete-data -y mrtest` — 0.212s real. I created TWO DISTINCT SERVER IDENTITIES with no browser, no SDK, and no spacetimedb.com round-trip, by giving each its own CLI config: `spacetimedb-cli --config-path=<dir>/cli.toml login --server-issued-login http://127.0.0.1:3999` → A=c20038d88e49c956cce82f430a27fde728f00788845bad263df006f87bb4c1fa, B=c200cef6ebd45bc78c09d997671538fd50adfd903a3389c862b1b85daf714fe3. Both called join_game (EXIT=0) and each got a starter monster (rows 1 and 2, owner_identity matching).
findings.source: Local execution against /home/mdrewt/.local/share/spacetime/bin/2.6.0/spacetimedb-cli (spacetimedb tool version 2.6.0, commit 31fd1c8c) using /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/projects/monster-realm/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/monster_realm_module.wasm
findings.caveat: Use `--config-path=<file>`, NOT `--root-dir`. `--root-dir` relocates the entire spacetime INSTALL (the wrapper then tries to exec <root>/bin/current/spacetimedb-cli and dies 'No such file or directory'). Also invoke the versioned binary directly to bypass the updater wrapper. Subcommand flags (-s) must come AFTER the subcommand; --config-path is a global and must come BEFORE it.

findings.claim: MEASURED: the guards the source-scans exist to pin ARE behaviourally testable this way — the reducer's Err(String) comes back verbatim with a non-zero exit code. Identity A calling `care 2` (B's monster) → stderr `Error: Response text: not owner`, EXIT=1. A calling `care 1` (own monster) → EXIT=0, and `spacetime sql` then shows trust_favorable_count 0→1 and last_care_at_ms 0→1786844522241. A calling `care 1` again immediately → `Error: Response text: care cooldown not yet elapsed`, EXIT=1. Single call latency: 0.018s real. This is a real behavioural proof of require_owner (server-module/src/guards.rs:63-74) and evaluate_care (server-module/src/raising.rs:61-66) executing inside a live reducer — the precise thing ADR-0156 P7 declares impossible.
findings.source: Local execution; guards at /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/projects/monster-realm/server-module/src/guards.rs:63 and .../raising.rs:61,98

findings.claim: MEASURED: privacy/RLS is testable too. The module owner's `spacetime sql` reads the PRIVATE `monster` table fine; identity A's identical query is refused with `Error: no such table: monster. If the table exists, it may be marked private.` (HTTP 400). So the must-never-leak table assertions currently proven by scanning schema.rs for the absence of the `public` keyword can be proven by a real denied query instead.
findings.source: Local execution against the published module; table declared at /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/projects/monster-realm/server-module/src/schema.rs

findings.claim: MEASURED LIMITATION, and it is the honest boundary of the CLI-only harness: after the one-shot HTTP calls returned, `SELECT identity, name, online FROM player` was EMPTY — on_disconnect deleted both player rows. Reducers gated on a live, still-connected counterparty (propose_trade requires a joined counterparty at trading.rs:246-250; PvP challenge; anything reading `player`) CANNOT be driven by `spacetime call` alone. Session-independent state (monster, inventory, wallet, evolution, config) survives and is fully reachable. This is exactly the objection ADR-0184 D1 raised when it rejected a scripts/ CLI harness — the objection is correct but narrower than 'a CLI harness does not work'.
findings.source: Local execution; ADR at /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/projects/monster-realm/docs/adr/0184-trade-negative-path-dynamic-suite.md (D1, 'Rejected — a scripts/ CLI harness'); precedent note scripts/smoke-republish.sh:37-39 (RT-SR-01)

findings.claim: The fix for that limitation is already a dependency of this repo, unused for testing: client/package.json declares `"spacetimedb": "^2.6.0"` (the official TS SDK) and client/src/module_bindings/ holds 64 generated binding files. A plain Node script (no Vite, no Playwright, no chromium, no DOM) can open and HOLD a WebSocket connection per identity, keeping the `player` row alive, and call reducers with typed args. ADR-0184 rejected a node-SDK harness on item-SEEDING and touches-scope grounds, not on feasibility.

findings.claim: CORRECTION to the brief's established context: evaluate_train and evaluate_care are NOT in game-core. They are pub(crate) fns in server-module/src/raising.rs (evaluate_care at :61, evaluate_train at :121), taking scalars/value-structs and returning Result<_, String>, delegating to game_core SSOT predicates (is_cooldown_ready, focus_train). The pattern to generalise is 'pure decision seam extracted next to the reducer, called before the irreversible write' (see raising.rs:231 'DECISION before SPEND'), not 'move it to game-core'.

findings.claim: Source-scanning IS a legitimate, named engineering category — architectural fitness-function / conformance testing — with mature tooling in every other ecosystem: ArchUnit (Java), NetArchTest (.NET), ArchUnitTS and dependency-cruiser and ESLint architectural rules (JS/TS), import-linter and deptry (Python). Rust's equivalents are thinner but real: tdymel/arch_test (rule-based module/use-relationship analysis, installable as a cargo subcommand or dev-dependency), plus cargo-deny for dependency policy and the type system / feature resolver for boundary enforcement (which this repo already uses well: workspace resolver="2" and the game-core `spacetimedb` feature gate proven by a feature-isolation eval).

findings.claim: THE LINE, stated precisely: a conformance rule is legitimate when its predicate is a property of the CODE ITSELF that no execution can observe, and it names the shape it forbids rather than the shape it requires. Legitimate: 'no module under server-module/src imports client code'; 'the game-core crate never enables the spacetimedb feature'; 'no OS-entropy or chrono call appears in a determinism-guarded crate'; 'every #[table] in schema.rs is baselined in table-schemas.json' (a schema/artifact-parity check, not a behaviour check); 'no reducer is #[cfg(feature=dev_reducers)] in a release build'. Illegitimate — a behavioural test in a regex costume: any rule whose failure mode is a WRONG ANSWER AT RUNTIME. 'require_owner is called in this reducer body' (the answer is: A gets B's monster); 'the == is not inverted at the authorize call site' (ADR-0184 caught exactly this: structural checkers verified field presence in the argument span and never the OPERATOR); 'evaluate_train is called before consume_one'; 'the reaper re-checks staleness'. Two diagnostics settle any borderline case: (1) can you write a semantically-correct refactor that FAILS the rule? then it is over-fitted to syntax; (2) can you write a semantically-BROKEN program that PASSES it? then it is a behavioural test wearing a costume — and ADR-0156 proves this repo has already built three such programs by hand. A third, decisive tell for this codebase: if satisfying the rule requires shaping production code (concat!() at accounts.rs:54 / pvp.rs:63), the rule has stopped describing the architecture and started dictating the text.
findings.source: Synthesis; evidence at docs/adr/0184-trade-negative-path-dynamic-suite.md (Context, ':433/:472 operator' finding) and docs/adr/0156-...md:244-276 (three evasions)

findings.claim: Community practice adds nothing beyond the official pattern. There is no third-party SpacetimeDB reducer-test framework on crates.io or GitHub; the ecosystem's answer is the same publish-and-drive loop plus 'unit test pure functions directly'. Clockwork's own flagship example (Blackholio) ships no module-level reducer test suite; its cross-language coverage requests live as open issues (#2172). This project's source-scan corpus is, as far as I can find, the most elaborate workaround anyone has built for this gap — which is a signal about the workaround, not a validation of it.

findings.caveat: Absence of evidence from a GitHub/web sweep is weaker than the direct API evidence above. Treat the 'nothing exists' half as INFERRED; the 'official pattern is publish-and-drive' half is from TESTING.md and is REPORTED-authoritative.

findings.claim: 2.6.0-specific gotchas that will bite whoever builds this: (1) `spacetime sql` on 2.6.0 has NO --format flag (--interactive, --confirmed, --anonymous, -s, -y, --no-config only) — the newer docs describing --format json apply to a later CLI; assertions must parse the ASCII table, or go through the HTTP endpoint POST /v1/database/:name/sql which returns JSON {schema, rows} directly. (2) `spacetime call` has no identity flag; identity comes from the config file, hence --config-path. (3) `spacetime login --server-issued-login <URL>` is present in the 2.6.0 binary but hidden from --help. (4) each reducer arg is its own JSON value, not a JSON array (ADR-0088 records this exact bug keeping a nightly job red). (5) `publish --bin-path` is required for dev_reducers because 2.6.0 publish has no cargo-feature passthrough (ADR-0054/ADR-0086).
findings.source: `spacetimedb-cli sql --help` / `call --help` / `login --help` run locally on 2.6.0; strings(1) on the binary for server-issued-login; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/master/docs/docs/13-HTTP%20API/03-database.md ; monster-realm scripts/smoke-republish.sh:52-56 ; client/e2e/global-setup.ts

research.recommendation:
RANKING: (b) FIRST, and it is not close — because (b) is 90% already built and the remaining 10% is measured at seconds, not minutes. Then (a) as the permanent companion. Then (d), rewritten in scope. (c) LAST / effectively NOT APPLICABLE.

The single most important correction to the project's own belief: ADR-0156 P7 and its four echoes (0117, 0138, 0168, 0170, 0185) say "there is no reducer-executing test harness." That is TRUE of in-crate Rust and FALSE of the repo as a whole. I built one today, from tools already on this machine and already in CI, and used it to prove `require_owner` and `evaluate_care` rejecting inside a live reducer: instance up in 2s, prebuilt wasm published in 0.212s, per-identity login via `--config-path`, reducer call 0.018s, rejection surfaced as EXIT=1 with the verbatim `Err(String)`, server truth read back through `spacetime sql`, and a non-owner's read of the private `monster` table refused. The blocker was never technical. It was that `--root-dir` (the obvious knob) is a trap and `--config-path` (the right one) is undocumented as an identity mechanism.

WHAT TO BUILD — one slice, small enough for a tier cap.
`ops/reducer-harness/` (or scripts/): a ~150-line bash+Node driver, plus one first suite.
  1. `up`: `spacetime start --in-memory --listen-addr 127.0.0.1:<port>`; wait for HTTP; `publish --bin-path $MR_DEV_MODULE_WASM --delete-data -y <ephemeral db>`. Reuse the CI block at ci.yml:149 verbatim.
  2. `identity <name>`: `spacetimedb-cli --config-path=$TMP/<name>/cli.toml login --server-issued-login $URL`. Call the VERSIONED binary directly (the `spacetime` wrapper mangles --root-dir); --config-path is a GLOBAL and goes before the subcommand, `-s` after it.
  3. `call <who> <reducer> <args...>` → assert exit code AND the stderr `Response text:` string. `expect_reject <who> <reducer> <args> <substring>` is the primitive the 6 blind security evals need.
  4. `sql <who> <query>` for server truth (2.6.0 has no --format json; either parse the table or POST /v1/database/:id/sql for real JSON).
  5. First suite: the six subsystems behind the blind security evals, negative paths only — battle, evolution, npc-dialogue-quest, raising, recruit, shop. Ownership, cooldown, battle-state and escrow guards are all reachable with session-independent state, which is what those six actually assert.

FOR THE SESSION-COUPLED CASES ONLY (propose_trade, PvP challenge, anything reading `player`): I measured that `on_disconnect` empties the `player` table after one-shot CLI calls, so those need a held connection. Do NOT reach for Playwright for them. `spacetimedb@^2.6.0` is already in client/package.json and 64 generated bindings already exist — a Node-only driver holding one WS per identity gets you multi-identity joined scenarios with no browser, no Vite, no chromium install. That is a SECOND, later slice; do not bundle it.

COST. Build: one small slice; the substrate is installed, pinned and CI-wired already, so there is no provisioning work and no new dependency. Runtime: instance 2s + publish 0.2s + ~0.02s/call means a 100-assertion suite runs in single-digit seconds against a prebuilt wasm — an order of magnitude cheaper than the existing Playwright e2e (45s timeouts, workers:1, full wasm+vite build). It should run in the fast `ci` job, not the heavy `e2e` job. Credit cost is dominated by the one authoring slice; steady-state cost is near zero and it should REDUCE spend by killing the source-scan authoring treadmill that produced 82,076 in-window insertions at 72.2% test+eval.

WHAT IT LETS YOU DELETE. 214 of 623 in-crate tests (34.3%), ~22,336 lines, are source-scan-touching. Do not delete them in the same slice — delete per-subsystem, only after the behavioural replacement is green, and only tests whose predicate is a runtime-observable fact. Highest-yield first: pvp_tests (38/50, ~3,936 lines), economy_tests (23/24, ~1,941), evolution_tests (15/41, ~3,012), battle_tests (22/48, ~2,591), trading_tests (16/38, ~2,016). Also retire the `concat!()` scanner-dodges at accounts.rs:54 and pvp.rs:63 — the only reason production code is shaped that way is a scanner that a behavioural test makes unnecessary. Expect the server-module mutation ratchet to improve as a side effect: justfile:94-96 explicitly attributes the 324-survivor cap to "the shell's reducers are covered by evals/integration/e2e rather than in-crate units," and ADR-0183 already names 11 in-crate-killable survivors.

WHAT (a) IS FOR. Keep extracting pure decision seams — but generalise the seam that actually exists (server-module/src/raising.rs:61,121, pure fn next to the reducer, called before the irreversible write at :231), NOT "move it to game-core." Be honest about its ceiling: after evaluate_care is extracted from `care`, what remains is require_owner, is_in_ongoing_battle, reject_if_monster_in_trade and the monster_pub dual-write — all DB-reading, all un-extractable, and all exactly what the security evals are trying to pin. (a) buys arithmetic coverage and cannot close the security gap. It is a companion to (b), never a substitute.

WHAT NOT TO DO.
- Do NOT build (c). ReducerContext is `#[non_exhaustive]` with no constructor, so a "test double" means a ports/adapters trait threaded through all 63 reducers — a rewrite of every reducer body to buy a weaker guarantee than (b) already gives, with the adapter (where the real bugs live) still untested. Reject it on evidence, not taste.
- Do NOT write another scanner. ADR-0184 already flagged "answering a no-dynamic-coverage finding with more source-text matching" as the anti-pattern, and ADR-0156 records an adversarial pass that kept the defect fully intact while every scan passed.
- Do NOT keep the 6 blind security evals (battle-, evolution-, npc-dialogue-quest-, raising-, recruit-, shop-reducer-security) on the raw scanner and call migrating them to rust-scan.mjs a fix. Migration makes a wrong-category test less wrong; it is a stopgap for one tick, not the remediation. 14r-c-2 owns these and exists nowhere on disk — this slice is its real home.
- Do NOT delete a scan until its behavioural replacement is green in CI, and do NOT delete scans whose predicate is genuinely architectural.

WHAT (d) BECOMES. Keep source-scanning, renamed and re-scoped to architectural conformance: rules whose predicate no execution can observe. Legitimate survivors — feature-isolation (game-core never enables `spacetimedb`), crate-boundary imports, the determinism bans on OS-entropy/chrono (ADR-0055), table-schema/type baseline parity against evals/baselines/*.json, dev_reducers absent from release. Everything of the form "guard X is called in body Y", "the operator is == not !=", "A is called before B" migrates to (b) and dies. Two tests to apply at review time: can a semantically-correct refactor fail this rule? (over-fitted to syntax) — and can a semantically-broken program pass it? (behavioural test in a regex costume). And the local tell: if satisfying the rule required editing production source into an unnatural shape, the rule is the defect.

SEQUENCING UNDER THE CREDIT CAP. This is one small, self-contained, high-PRIMARY-axis slice with no new dependencies and a measured proof-of-concept already in hand — exactly the shape that survives D4's decomposition target. Do not start it in the same tick as a deletion pass; the deletions are separate, per-subsystem, and each is trivially small. Under D1 pressure, defer the whole thing rather than shrink it: a half-built harness that has replaced nothing is the worst possible resting state.
unknowns: I did not verify that a Node-only process using spacetimedb@2.6.0 + the committed bindings can hold a live connection outside a browser (no DOM/WebSocket shim issues). The dependency and bindings exist; the headless-Node connection itself is UNTESTED and is the one real risk in the second slice.

The item/currency SEEDING problem ADR-0184 D4 records is untouched by any of this. A CLI-driven identity still cannot be given items by any shipping path, so shop/trade positive paths needing inventory may still need dev_reducers (grant_bait exists; a general faucet does not) — scope this explicitly before promising shop coverage.
I did not measure how many of the 214 scan-touching tests have a predicate that is genuinely architectural and must survive. My 34.3% is an upper bound on what is deletable, not a delete list.

Whether reducer rejections are distinguishable from transport/infra failures purely by exit code: both surfaced as EXIT=1 in my run. The harness must assert on the `Response text:` substring, not the exit code alone, or a server crash will read as a passing negative test — a vacuous-green risk of exactly the kind this repo already guards against elsewhere.

Scheduled reducers (movement_tick, the four reapers) are driven by the scheduler, not by callers. I did not test whether their bodies are reachable from this harness; they may need a time-advance affordance or stay on conformance rules. ADR-0117:51 already accepts live mutants in reaper bodies for this reason.

Whether `spacetime start --in-memory` is safe to run concurrently with the existing long-lived instance on :3111 in CI/local (port and data-dir isolation looked fine in my run on :3999, but I did not test parallel publishes to the same server).

designs.workstream: WS2 — Backlog integrity: making discovery reach a queue (RF-3). Deliverables: a machine-readable residual registry with an enforced emission point and real consumers; a mechanical ready-set (mr-ready) subordinate to the pacing gate; seeding from the supplied triage; a verdict on the boyscout allowance; retirement of obsolete residual prose; and the kill-switch provenance/placement split.

alternatives.name: A. Minimal — mr-ready only, no registry (do-nothing on RF-3 proper)
alternatives.sketch: Build ONLY the ready-set script. mr-ready parses the 108 `### <slice> —` headings in specs/monster-realm-v2/*.md for inline `touches:`/`after:`, derives the done-set from `**Slice:**` headers across docs/adr/*.md (MEASURED: present on 171 lines / 165 files), subtracts in-flight from $MEM/.harness-runner.*.lock, and prints a JSON ready-set. Residual discovery stays ADR prose. The supplied triage is committed once as a static markdown backlog that a human re-triages when it rots.
alternatives.pros: Smallest possible diff (one new ~150-line read-only script, ALWAYS rc=0, same contract as mr-disjoint). Kills the measured hourly waste of re-deriving priority from 390 lines of PLAN §9 prose. Zero risk to master CI, zero new format for any agent to learn, no change to the brief. Immediately usable: the done-set signal already exists and is free.
alternatives.cons: Does not touch RF-3 at all. Discovery still has no sink, so the 13.1-day disclosure→remediation latency and the orphan class (14r-c-2, 13r-c-2, pt-b1b, uxd3-d, pt-c2c, M-postgate-recruit-box-server-pin — all MEASURED to exist in no spec/PLAN/state file) reproduce on the next 100 ADRs. The static backlog is a snapshot with a decay half-life; the triage that produced it cost a large research pass and would have to be repaid.
alternatives.credit_impact: Cheapest to build (one S slice). Saves a little per tick. Guarantees the expensive re-triage recurs — negative over a quarter.
alternatives.quality_impact: Neutral-to-slightly-positive on scheduling; zero on the PRIMARY axis (testability/changeability), because the security exposures the triage found still have no mechanical path to a slice.

alternatives.name: B. GitHub Issues as the registry (the established answer)
alternatives.sketch: Adopt Google's documented TODO rule literally — the in-file tag carries only a tracker reference, the tracker holds the state. Each residual becomes a GitHub issue on mdrewt/monster-realm with labels (severity/domain/owning-slice); ADR prose keeps a one-line pointer `residual: #NNN`. Closure is free and automatic via `Closes #NNN` in the PR body. Dedup via issue search. mr-ready and mr-situation read `gh issue list --label residual --json`. The mr-ask-drew machinery already proves the channel works and is push-notified to the operator's phone.
alternatives.pros: Established, off-the-shelf, and directly matches the primary source (google.github.io/styleguide: "A bug reference is preferable because bugs are tracked and have follow-up comments"). Zero code for storage, state machine, dedup or closure. Operator can triage from anywhere. PEP 350's rejection is the warning against inventing a grammar; this avoids it entirely.
alternatives.cons: Three disqualifying frictions, all local. (1) CHANNEL DESTRUCTION: the issue list is already the operator's DECISION channel (mr-ask-drew, doctrine line 81, plus the #11/#12 incident rule that "an open issue whose answer was consumed is a lie to Drew's issue list"). Seeding ~295 outstanding rows floods a working, low-volume, human-read channel with backlog noise. (2) WRONG AUTHORING MOMENT: residuals are discovered inside a detached headless run that is deliberately forbidden from mutating anything outside its worktree; `gh issue create` per residual adds a mutating network call with auth/rate-limit failure modes to the one process that must never wedge. (3) INVISIBLE TO THE GAUNTLET: an issue is created outside the diff, so the reviewer/red-team/verifier lenses — the mechanism MEASURED to work (93 runs, found a merge-blocker before code existed) — cannot see or challenge the row. A residual that no lens reads is the graveyard again, relocated.
alternatives.credit_impact: Low build cost, but every future slice pays network calls and the operator pays attention-tax on a polluted channel. The attention cost is the one the operator explicitly asked to reduce (D5).
alternatives.quality_impact: Good state machine, poor review coupling. Line-anchored residuals (e.g. "battle.rs:1050, drifted from ~944") rot invisibly because the issue is not versioned with the code.

alternatives.name: C. ADR-native generated registry — extend scripts/adr-digest.mjs (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: The residual's SSOT is a canonical row inside the ADR that already must be written; the queryable artifact is generated. Concretely: (i) a `## Residuals` block with one machine-readable row per item (`- R-0193-1 | sev=HIGH | domain=security | touches=<globs> | dup-of=— | <one line>`), parsed by the extractors that already exist (extractListField at scripts/adr-digest.mjs:136); (ii) generation of docs/adr/residuals.json beside the existing docs/adr/design-corpus.json and DIGEST.md by the same `main()` write at scripts/adr-digest.mjs:864; (iii) closure via a `**Closes:**` header field validated relationally by the checkRefs/validateBacklinks machinery already at :509 — a dangling `Closes:` is already an error class; (iv) the ~295 legacy rows from the supplied triage seeded into ONE file, docs/adr/residuals-seed.json, exactly mirroring design-corpus.json's role as a companion corpus the generator merges; (v) an era cutoff RESIDUAL_ERA_MIN plus a monotone-shrinking legacy set with a rot detector, copied verbatim from the KNOWN_BACKLINK_GAPS ratchet at :55-96.
alternatives.pros: Every mechanism it needs ALREADY EXISTS AND RUNS IN CI (MEASURED: 871-line parser, per-ADR validator :242, cross-ADR relational validator :509, controlled vocabulary :22, malformed-key exit-2 guard :83-93, `just adr-digest-check` at justfile:239 wired through evals/adr-digest.eval.mjs). The row is IN THE DIFF, so the reviewer/red-team/verifier gauntlet reads it — the only design where discovery is challenged at creation. Versioned with the code, so line anchors move with the file. No network. The ADR is on the WHAT-IS-WORKING list (143 ADRs cited 3,729 times); this fixes the Residuals-as-graveyard pattern without touching what works.
alternatives.cons: ~200 lines of new parsing/validation in an existing file, plus a real risk of the 2h11m master-red class if the generated artifact's freshness check is enforced from day one (the existing DIGEST.md staleness check already produced exactly that incident). Mitigated by shipping the residual half of `--check` in WARN for a stated promotion period (Gatekeeper dryrun→warn→enforce) and by keeping the ENFORCEMENT of emission at mr-audit, where a false positive costs an adjudication and can never red master.
alternatives.credit_impact: One M slice for the generator, one M for the seed, one S for closure. Marginal per-slice authoring cost is ~1 line inside a document the doc-keeper is already writing. Pays for itself the first time it prevents one re-triage.
alternatives.quality_impact: Highest on the PRIMARY axis: it is the only option where a named security exposure (14r-c-2's 6 blind evals; ADR-0042's world-readable `battle` table) becomes a row a scheduler can see, and where the residual is adversarially reviewed at the moment it is written.

alternatives.name: D. Standalone append-only backlog file (docs/backlog.jsonl), hand-edited
alternatives.sketch: A single JSONL file in the project repo, appended by the build session at park/merge time, closed by appending a terminal row. mr-ready reads it directly. No generator, no ADR coupling.
alternatives.pros: Simplest data model; append-only matches the ledger pattern the loop already uses successfully (monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl). One file to read, trivially parseable.
alternatives.cons: A single hot file that EVERY slice must append to is a new always-serial structural surface — it collides with the fan-out mechanism that MEASURED-works (mr-disjoint's STRUCTURAL list exists precisely for this class), and it is not in the existing STRUCTURAL globs so collisions would go undetected. It also decouples the row from the ADR that justifies it, so a reader gets an assertion with no rationale — re-creating the problem where 78 defer phrases were unreadable prose. And it duplicates a corpus/generator pattern the repo already has two working instances of.
alternatives.credit_impact: Cheap to build, expensive in serialization: every slice touching it forces serial fan-out.
alternatives.quality_impact: Negative on changeability — it makes concurrent slices collide on a bookkeeping file.

designs.chosen: C — the ADR-native generated registry, with two properties deliberately borrowed from B (the closure-keyword semantics `Closes:`, and Google's rule that the in-prose form is a POINTER carrying an ID, never the store). DECISIVE REASON, on the PRIMARY axis: option C is the only one where a residual is created inside the diff and therefore passes under the reviewer/red-team/verifier gauntlet that is MEASURED to work. RF-3 is not a storage problem — it is a problem of discovery that no reader reads; B relocates the graveyard to a channel no lens inspects and pollutes the operator's decision channel, D creates an undeclared always-serial file, and A leaves RF-3 untouched. On value-per-credit, C is also the cheapest of the three real options because the generator, the per-ADR validator, the cross-ADR relational validator, the controlled-vocabulary pattern, the malformed-key exit-2 guard, the monotone-shrinking legacy ratchet, and the CI wiring ALL ALREADY EXIST in scripts/adr-digest.mjs and run today — this is one new list field plus one new generated artifact in a parser that already parses every ADR in CI, not a new system. SUBORDINATE CALLS: (1) the boyscout allowance needs no work and must NOT be widened — it already exists in mr-brief-template.md at ~40 lines/≤3 hunks, is scoped WITHIN declared touches: so it is invisible to mr-disjoint by construction (doctrine line 95, verified in mr-disjoint's own header), and the research found the boyscout literature is folklore with no controlled evidence; the only change is that out-of-cap cleanup becomes a registry row instead of a handoff note; (2) enforcement lives at mr-audit (supervisor-side, pre-merge), NOT master CI, so it structurally cannot reproduce the 2h11m docs-only red, and it takes the slot vacated by gating_test_audit (0 true positives in 446 v3-era rows — an effective-FP rate an order of magnitude past Google's documented <10% abandonment threshold), keeping mr-audit at exactly two checks.

steps.title: Residual row grammar + residuals.json emission in the existing ADR generator

This is deliberately the same asymmetry as mr-disjoint (may downgrade toward serial, never upgrade toward parallel).

The brief's TARGET_DESC construction is untouched; BL-7 adds exactly one line to it.

DO-NOT-RETRY #10/#11 — tokens-per-line-added and remediation-share-of-spend as KPIs. Both are gameable by emitting more output, and the loop's output channel is already saturated (82,076 in-window insertions, 173 total production deletions). The success metrics here are disclosure→registry LATENCY (0 days by construction post-cutoff) and ORPHAN COUNT (named work resolving in no artifact), neither of which improves by producing more lines.

Reinventing a residual grammar and hoping tooling follows — the documented PEP 350 dead end. The in-prose row is deliberately minimal (id + five closed-vocabulary fields + one 140-char line); every richer structure lives in the generated artifact.

Building a new registry system when the repo already has two working corpus+generator instances (DIGEST.md and design-corpus.json). BL-1/BL-2 add a field and a companion file to a 871-line parser that already runs in CI, rather than a new subsystem.

A hot append-only backlog file (alternative D) that every slice must touch — an undeclared always-serial surface invisible to mr-disjoint's STRUCTURAL list, which would silently degrade the fan-out mechanism that measurably works.

The research found the boyscout literature is folklore with no controlled evidence, and Google's own carve-out is rename-scale. It is a complement, not a sink — 6 blind security evals is a slice, not litter. Only change: out-of-cap cleanup becomes a registry row.

BL-6 puts the refusal in mr-spawn — the sole launch path — with NO env override at all, so a forced manual run is structurally incapable of launching while remaining capable of draining.

designs.workstream: Workstream 3 — Test architecture: the missing reducer harness and the end of source-scanning

alternatives.name: A. Minimal — harden the scanners in place, no new capability
alternatives.sketch: Accept that source-scanning is the permanent testing substrate. Migrate the 7 KNOWN_UNMIGRATED evals (evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:137-185) onto evals/rust-scan.mjs, migrate trade-escrow-guards + trade-conservation (13r-c-2), delete the concat!() splits at server-module/src/accounts.rs:54 and server-module/src/pvp.rs:63, wire nightly failure notification, wire ops/observability/validate.mjs. Change nothing about the 46,434-line Rust test corpus or the 120 source-reading sites.
alternatives.pros: Smallest credit spend by a wide margin (~4-5 small slices). Closes the live security exposure (6 blind evals) and the M21b-2 deploy gate immediately. Every step is independently valuable and none can break the working brief/gauntlet/fan-out machinery. Fixes the two escaped-defect classes (silent nightly red, container crash-loop) for near-zero cost.
alternatives.cons: Does not close the root defect. ADR-0156's own adversarial pass built a tree where the defect was fully intact and EVERY server-side scan passed; migrating a scanner makes a wrong-category test less wrong, not right. Leaves the 173-production-deletions / 72.2%-test-lines dynamic untouched — the scan corpus keeps growing because it is the only place assertions can live. Leaves pvp_tests.rs:497-518 style tests (assert a broken STRING is absent) as the primary proof for security guards; any benign rename makes them vacuously green.
alternatives.credit_impact: Lowest. ~4-5 tier-cap-sized slices total.
alternatives.quality_impact: Materially positive on the acute items, zero on the structural one. Rediscovery rate stays where it is.

alternatives.name: B. Extract-to-pure-seams — push guards into game-core, let mutate-core cover them
alternatives.sketch: Generalise the raising.rs pattern (evaluate_care :61 / evaluate_train :121 — pure decision seam beside the reducer, called before the irreversible write at :231) and the game-core/src/trading/rules.rs pattern (check_headroom :404, authorize_respond :444, authorize_confirm :459). Move every extractable predicate into game-core so the zero-tolerance mutate-core gate (justfile:68) covers it automatically; the residual source-scan degrades to a one-line 'does the reducer still call the seam' needle.
alternatives.pros: No new infrastructure, no new dependency, no CI runtime. Rides an existing zero-tolerance mutation gate. Directly serves the operator's testability/changeability priority. The template is already in-tree and proven: raising_tests.rs is 54 tests / 1 scan against pvp_tests.rs 51 tests / 28 scans.
alternatives.cons: Has a hard, measured ceiling and cannot reach the security surface. After evaluate_care is extracted from `care` (server-module/src/raising.rs:74-116), what REMAINS is exactly require_owner(ctx,..), is_in_ongoing_battle(ctx,..), reject_if_monster_in_trade(ctx.db..) and the monster_pub dual-write — all DB-reading, all un-extractable, and all precisely what the 6 blind security evals exist to pin. So it buys arithmetic coverage and leaves the security-guard class exactly as untested as today. Also drags game-core/** into every touch set, colliding with mr-disjoint's serial content list.
alternatives.credit_impact: Medium, and open-ended — a per-slice habit with no terminal state.
alternatives.quality_impact: Good but bounded. Cannot retire a single security scan.

alternatives.name: C. New Node/TS-SDK integration harness
alternatives.sketch: Write a headless Node driver against client/package.json's existing `spacetimedb: ^2.6.0` dependency and the 64 committed files in client/src/module_bindings/, holding one WebSocket per identity, calling reducers with typed args and asserting on rejection strings.
alternatives.pros: Typed reducer args from generated bindings. Dependency already declared. Node is already installed in both CI jobs.
alternatives.cons: REJECTED ON EVIDENCE: it re-buys a capability the repo already owns. It also imports a bindings-regeneration coupling (`spacetime generate` drift becomes a harness-breaking event), puts the harness in the client's npm blast radius, and the headless-Node connection path is explicitly UNTESTED per the research unknowns. ADR-0184 D1 already rejected a variant of this. Worst of all it splits the assertion substrate across two languages while server-module/src/*_tests.rs stays Rust.
alternatives.credit_impact: High — new code, new failure modes, an untested connection path to de-risk first.
alternatives.quality_impact: Equivalent end-state to D at strictly higher cost and risk.

alternatives.name: D. Promote the in-repo WS client to a reducer-conformance harness (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: Extract the SpacetimeDB WS/HTTP client already living inside sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs into a reusable sim-harness lib module; add server→client response capture (drain_feed at :1784 currently parses frame headers and discards payloads) so a reducer's Err(String) is readable; then write behavioural negative-path suites for the six subsystems whose security evals are blind, run them in the EXISTING ci.yml e2e job substrate, and delete the scan tests they replace — one subsystem per slice, deletion paired with replacement. Keep source-scanning only for genuine architectural-conformance rules.
alternatives.pros: The capability is ~80% built and dependency-free (sim-harness/Cargo.toml deps = game-core only): identity minting (:2183), held WS per identity (:2219 — solves the on_disconnect/player-row limitation that defeats a CLI-only harness), CallReducer construction (:2089), bearer HTTP for the JSON /sql endpoint (:1890), frame parsing (:1695/:1784), all already unit-tested in-file. The CI substrate exists at ci.yml:120-149 (pinned 2.6.0, dev_reducers wasm, in-memory instance) so there is zero provisioning work. Directly refutes ADR-0156 P7 / 0168:208 / 0170:293 / 0185:121 — the word to challenge in all five is IN-PROCESS, true of in-crate Rust and false of the repo. It is the only option that makes the ~214 scan-touching tests DELETABLE, which is the only real simplification pressure available.
alternatives.cons: Requires a real (if small) new capability and CI runtime. Cannot reach scheduled reducers (movement_tick, the four reapers) without a time-advance affordance. Item/currency seeding still needs dev_reducers for shop/trade positive paths (ADR-0184 D4's unsolved problem). Exit status alone cannot distinguish a reducer rejection from a transport failure, so assertions must pin the response string or the suite is vacuously green.
alternatives.credit_impact: Medium overall, front-loaded into two small slices (extract, then response-capture) each with an unambiguous falsification test. Steady-state cost is near zero and it should REDUCE spend by ending the scan-authoring treadmill.
alternatives.quality_impact: Highest available. Converts the largest standing gate gap from structural to behavioural and creates the first genuine deletion pressure in the loop.

alternatives.name: E. ReducerContext test double
alternatives.sketch: Construct a fake ReducerContext (or thread a ports/adapters trait through the reducers) so reducer bodies execute under cargo nextest.
alternatives.pros: Would give in-crate, in-process, zero-runtime coverage if it worked.
alternatives.cons: STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE per the supplied research: ReducerContext is #[non_exhaustive] with no `new`, no `Default` and no test constructor, so it cannot be built from an external crate; and spacetimedb-bindings-sys is the wasm host-ABI shim, so any test touching ctx.db pulls in #[link(wasm_import_module=..)] externs. The trait-threading variant rewrites all 63 reducer bodies to buy a WEAKER guarantee than D — the adapter, where the real bugs live, stays untested. Upstream issues #2833 and #2788 are open, unanswered, with no proposed API.
alternatives.credit_impact: Very high (a rewrite of every reducer).
alternatives.quality_impact: Negative relative to D — more churn, weaker proof.

designs.chosen: D, sequenced behind the acute items from A. The decisive reason is a measured fact that inverts the project's own five-times-repeated conclusion: the repo ALREADY OWNS a working, dependency-free SpacetimeDB WebSocket client that mints N distinct identities and holds a live connection per identity (sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs:2183, :2219, :2089, :1890, :1784), and CI already installs, pins and runs the exact substrate it needs (.github/workflows/ci.yml:120-149). ADR-0156 P7 and its four echoes call the reducer-execution gap unbuildable; that claim is true of in-crate Rust and false of this repository. Option D is therefore not a new capability purchase — it is an extraction plus a response-read, the cheapest possible route to the operator's PRIMARY axis. On value-per-credit it also wins uniquely: it is the only alternative that makes the ~214 scan-touching tests (34.3% of 623, roughly 22,000 lines) DELETABLE, and deletion is the only honest answer to the 173-production-deletions / 72.2%-test-lines dynamic. B is kept as a companion habit, not a substitute — after evaluate_care is extracted, the entire remaining surface of `care` (raising.rs:74-116) is DB-reading guards no pure seam can reach. A's items ship FIRST regardless: they are live exposure (6 blind security evals) and a hard deploy gate (13r-c-2), and S1/S2 close two defect classes that actually escaped for almost no credit.

steps.title: Extract the SpacetimeDB WS/HTTP client from the load-driver binary into a sim-harness lib module

No behaviour change, no new dependency (sim-harness/Cargo.toml stays deps = game-core only). This is the whole reason D is cheap — the client, the identity minting and the held connection already exist and are already tested.
