steps.title: Add reducer-response capture — read the Err(String) back off the socket
steps.files: sim-harness/src/stdb_client.rs (drain_feed, which today sets state.skip_remaining and discards data payloads at the :1784-1846 logic); new fn call_reducer_await; new fn expect_reject
steps.change: Extend drain_feed with a capture mode buffering text-frame payloads instead of skipping them, and add `call_reducer_await(stream, reducer, args, request_id, timeout) -> Result<(), String>` which sends a CallReducer and reads frames until it sees a TransactionUpdate whose request_id matches, returning Ok(()) on committed and Err(reason) on failed. The assertion primitive the blind evals need is `expect_reject(who, reducer, args, substring)`. CRITICAL: assert on the response STRING, never on a bare success/failure bit — a transport error and a reducer rejection are otherwise indistinguishable and the suite goes vacuously green on a server crash.
steps.verification: Two live assertions against a local instance: identity A calling `care` on identity B's monster returns Err containing 'not owner' (proving require_owner at server-module/src/guards.rs:63-74 executes); A calling `care` twice on its own monster returns Err containing 'care cooldown not yet elapsed' (proving evaluate_care at raising.rs:61-66 executes). Both must FAIL if the guard is deleted from the reducer — verify by deleting it locally once.
steps.risk: Frame reassembly across fragmented/continuation frames is the classic bug; drain_feed already handles opcode 0x0 continuation, so extend rather than rewrite. Timeout handling must fail loud, never fall through to Ok.
steps.rollback: Revert the capture mode; drain_feed returns to skip-only and the load driver is unaffected (it never reads payloads).

steps.title: First reducer-conformance suite: the six subsystems whose security evals are blind
steps.files: new sim-harness/src/bin/mr_reducer_conformance.rs; .github/workflows/ci.yml (new step inside the EXISTING e2e job, after 'Wait for SpacetimeDB' at :116-124, reusing the already-built dev_reducers wasm from :143)
steps.change: A negative-path suite per subsystem — battle, evolution, npc-dialogue-quest, raising, recruit, shop — asserting ownership, cooldown, battle-state and escrow guards via expect_reject with the exact reason string, plus privacy assertions via `POST /v1/database/<db>/sql` under a non-owner bearer token (a private table must be refused, not returned). Start with negative paths only: they need no item seeding, which is ADR-0184 D4's unsolved problem. Scheduled reducers (movement_tick, the four reapers) are OUT OF SCOPE — scheduler-driven, they stay on conformance rules.
steps.verification: Delete one guard from one reducer locally and confirm the suite REDs with a message naming that guard. Every assertion carries this red-first proof, per the existing proof-of-teeth discipline — a gate that has never failed is a decoration. Also assert total runtime: the suite must complete in single-digit seconds against a prebuilt wasm (measured per-call latency ~0.02s), or it belongs in nightly rather than per-PR.
steps.risk: The one L. Split it if it breaks the cap: land battle+raising first (highest scan concentration), then the other four. Do NOT let it grow to cover positive paths in the same slice.
steps.rollback: Delete the binary and the CI step; the extracted client stays and remains useful to the load driver.

steps.title: Retire behavioural-costume scan tests — one subsystem per slice, deletion paired with replacement
steps.files: server-module/src/pvp_tests.rs (28 scans / 51 tests, 4807 lines — including :497-518 rt_m16_02, which asserts a BROKEN STRING is absent and can never prove the correct operator is present); evolution_tests.rs (15/42); content_cache_tests.rs (12/28); battle_tests.rs (11/51); economy_tests.rs (10/24)
steps.change: Per subsystem, delete only those scan tests whose predicate is a RUNTIME-OBSERVABLE FACT now proven behaviourally by S8. Classification rule applied per test — KEEP if the predicate is a property of the code no execution can observe: a table must never be declared `public`; a reducer must not be cfg-gated in a release build; game-core must never enable the spacetimedb feature; no OS-entropy/chrono call in a determinism-guarded crate; every #[table] is baselined in table-schemas.json. DELETE if failure means a WRONG ANSWER AT RUNTIME: 'require_owner is called in this body', 'the operator is == not !=', 'evaluate_train is called before consume_one', 'the practice flag is not computed with != WILD_IDENTITY'. Two review diagnostics settle borderline cases: (1) can a semantically-correct refactor fail this rule? then it is over-fitted to syntax; (2) can a semantically-broken program pass it? then it is a behavioural test in a regex costume — and ADR-0156 records three such programs already built by hand.
steps.verification: For each deleted test, the S8 assertion replacing it must be named in the slice's ADR and must have been demonstrated RED against the same injected defect. Net production+test line delta is recorded in the ADR header — recorded, NOT gated, because a line-count budget is gameable in both directions and the research found no credible prior art for one.
steps.risk: Deleting a scan whose behavioural replacement does not cover the same defect. Mitigated absolutely by the rule that no scan is deleted before its replacement is green in CI AND has been shown to red on the injected defect. Upper bound on deletable material is ~214 of 623 tests / ~22,000 lines — a ceiling, not a target.
steps.rollback: Per-subsystem revert restores the scan tests; the behavioural suite is additive and stays.

steps.title: Mutation gate: advisory changed-lines signal + per-module RATE ratchet + named-debt list — MUST BE ONE SLICE
steps.files: justfile:110 (`mutate-server cap="324"`), :138 (`missed=$(grep -c '' mutants.out/missed.txt)`), :85 (`missed=$(wc -l < ...)` in mutate-core — undercounts a newline-less last line, a vacuous-green on the strictest gate); evals/nightly-smoke-wiring.eval.mjs:323 (MUTATE_SERVER_CAP_BASELINE), :416/:418 (incomplete scope-narrowing ban list); .github/workflows/ci.yml (new advisory job)
steps.change: Three changes that cannot be split because the cap and its eval baseline are pinned to exact equality. (1) Replace the absolute survivor cap with a per-module survival RATE (missed/(missed+caught)) read from mutants.out/outcomes.json — the absolute cap is calibrated finer than the tool's own reproducibility (ADR-0183 records 323 local vs 324 hosted on a semantically identical tree; as a rate that is 42.90% vs 43.03%). (2) Carry the 11 ADR-0183-named killable survivors as a monotone-shrinking named-debt list copying the ratchet already working at scripts/adr-digest.mjs:55-96 (era cutoff, a set that MAY ONLY SHRINK, a frozen duplicate asserting set equality so growth needs two visible edits, a malformed-key validator, a rot detector that errors when a listed item is already fixed). (3) Add an ADVISORY per-PR `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <pr.diff> --annotations github` job with mandatory triage — NOT a blocker, because the diff is matched only against code under test (a PR that guts tests generates zero mutants and reads green), and because zero tolerance forces either implementation-pinning assertions or skip attributes in production source. Also normalise mutate-core onto `grep -c ''` and widen the ban list to every cargo-mutants scope-narrowing flag including short forms (-e/-E/-f/-F, --in-diff, --iterate, --exclude, --skip-calls, --test-package, --baseline), each with a BAD fixture proving it bites.
steps.verification: Feed the rate ratchet a synthetic outcomes.json where the population grows 47% while survival improves 15 points (the measured 513/299 → 753/324 case) and confirm it stays GREEN — the absolute cap misread exactly this as a regression and fired 5 red nights. Then feed a rate regression and confirm RED. One BAD fixture per banned flag. For mutate-core, a one-survivor-no-trailing-newline missed.txt must RED (today `wc -l` returns 0 → vacuous green).
steps.risk: Getting the rate denominator wrong — unviable and timeout mutants must be excluded from the denominator, not counted as caught. Read one real outcomes.json before writing the parser; the book confirms the file holds summary counts but does not document the schema.
steps.rollback: Restore the cap constant in justfile and the baseline in the eval together; both must move in lockstep or the exact-equality assertion reds, which is the intended safety.

steps.title: Gates for the two remaining escaped classes: reducer latency and subscription payload size
steps.files: sim-harness/src/stdb_client.rs (reuse http_get_request → /v1/metrics, already implemented at :1907 and used by scrape_once :2169); new ceiling table beside game-core/benches/budgets.rs; .github/workflows/nightly.yml
steps.change: Add a nightly assertion on spacetime_txn_elapsed_time_sec{reducer=...} p95 per reducer against a ceiling derived from a fresh measurement, and on the byte size of the initial subscription payload for a fresh identity — the client subscribes 21 tables in ONE .subscribe array at client/src/net/connection.ts:690-751, several world-readable, so that number is a real and currently unmeasured regression surface. Do NOT tighten the existing criterion ceilings in game-core/benches/budgets.rs: the ~20x figure is the correct call for a wall-clock benchmark on a shared runner and the file documents why at :12-14; tightening buys flake, not sensitivity. If a tight ceiling is ever needed the answer is instruction counting (gungraun, formerly iai-callgrind), not a smaller multiplier.
steps.verification: Record each ceiling with its measured value, date and conditions in the AM11 provenance style already used at budgets.rs:24-33. Falsification: inject an artificial 10x delay in one reducer path locally and confirm the latency gate reds; add 5 tables to the subscription array and confirm the payload gate reds.
steps.risk: Hosted-runner variance makes p95 latency noisy; set the first ceiling generously and ratchet from observed data rather than guessing. Frame time is deliberately NOT proposed — it needs a rendering harness that does not exist and no escaped defect traces to it.
steps.rollback: Delete the nightly job; no production code touched.

antipatterns_avoided: DO-NOT-RETRY #4 — raising the absolute mutation survivor cap. S10 replaces the absolute cap entirely with a per-module survival RATE plus a monotone-shrinking named-debt list, and its falsification test is specifically the measured 513/299 → 753/324 case where population grew 47% while the rate improved 15 points and the absolute cap fired 5 false red nights.
DO-NOT-RETRY #1 — costwatch_enforce as a kill. Nothing here kills or strands a run; the mutation signal is explicitly ADVISORY with mandatory triage, not a blocker.
DO-NOT-RETRY #3 — raising duty cycle / N_MAX / cron frequency. No throughput lever anywhere; every step is a per-slice quality change.
DO-NOT-RETRY #5 — the fable-vs-opus A/B. Not proposed; the quality instruments are still dead and an A/B on dead instruments yields the predictable wrong conclusion.

DO-NOT-RETRY #10 and #11 — tokens-per-line-added and remediation-share-of-spend as KPIs. S9 records net line delta in the ADR header but explicitly does NOT gate on it, because a line-count budget is gameable in both directions and the research found no credible prior art for one.
DO-NOT-RETRY #12 — an ADR defer-phrase denylist as a blocking gate. Not proposed.

A ReducerContext test double (option E). Refused on the supplied evidence, not on taste: ReducerContext is #[non_exhaustive] with no constructor, bindings-sys is the wasm host ABI, and the ports/adapters variant rewrites all 63 reducers to buy a weaker guarantee than S8 while leaving the adapter untested.

Answering a no-dynamic-coverage finding with MORE source-text matching — the anti-pattern ADR-0184 already named. S3/S4 migrate scanners only as acute triage for live exposure; S9 retires the behavioural-costume category rather than improving it.

A big-bang rewrite of the 46,434-line Rust test corpus. S9 is strictly per-subsystem, deletion is paired with a demonstrated-red replacement, and the ~214-test / ~22,000-line figure is stated as a ceiling, not a target.

Deleting scan tests before their behavioural replacement exists — trading a weak gate for no gate. Hard-sequenced: S9 depends on S8, and no scan may be deleted until its replacement has been shown RED on the injected defect.

Landing the concat!() deletion before the scanner migration. S5 depends on S4 for exactly this reason: a bare literal against the unmigrated whole-crate blob re-inverts quote polarity and blanks later files — a FALSE GREEN on a security gate, strictly worse than the dodge.

Tightening the criterion perf ceilings from ~20x. The research classifies this NOT_APPLICABLE as a defect: 20x is honest for wall-clock benchmarking on a shared runner, and tightening buys flake. S11 adds NEW ceilings for classes with no gate at all rather than sharpening one that is correctly calibrated.

Zero-tolerance mutation on the changed-lines signal, which would force implementation-pinning assertions or #[mutants::skip] attributes into production source — the same disease as the concat!() dodge. S10 keeps it advisory.

Adding #[mutants::skip] or new exclude_re entries as a way to move the number. The existing .cargo/mutants.toml (3 line-pinned entries, each with a proof of equivalence, one already retired when it stopped being equivalent) is exemplary and its bar is preserved.

Building a Node/TS-SDK or Playwright-based reducer harness (option C). Rejected because the repo already owns a dependency-free WS client with identity minting and held connections, and because a browser is not needed to call a reducer.
Bundling the 12-copy strip_rust_comments dedup (ADR-0186 D7) into the security migration — a 12-file blast radius with zero EARS progress that would swamp a security slice.

Shortening the per-slice brief, touching the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet, or narrowing mr-disjoint's structural always-serial list. All three are on the WHAT IS WORKING list and none is modified; S9 also deliberately keeps game-core/** off the critical path partly to avoid colliding with the serial content list.

Proposing scheduled-reducer (movement_tick, the four reapers) coverage in S8. They are scheduler-driven, need a time-advance affordance that does not exist, and ADR-0117:51 already accepts live mutants there — scoping them in would turn an M into an unbounded L.
Treating a `skipped` validator run as a pass in S1 — the exact vacuous-green shape this repo guards against elsewhere; validate.mjs already distinguishes the two at :115-121 and CI must honour it.

designs.workstream: WS4 — Supervisor-side gate stack and scheduling correctness (mr-audit gating half, CENSUS, human-activity probe, mr-disjoint, worktree isolation, reboot-path liveness, ledger integrity)

alternatives.name: A. Minimal triage — delete the flag, repoint the census, exclude .codegraph
alternatives.sketch: Three surgical edits, no new files, no new state. (1) Delete mr-audit:58-59 (unconditional hard-tier flag) and change :60 so the counters are REPORTED but never produce FLAGGED — gating becomes a data block, the supervisor stops paying a full-diff read. (2) mr-native-tick.sh:323 greps /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log instead of $TLOG. (3) Add `-not -path '*/.codegraph/*'` at mr-native-tick.sh:244. Nothing else changes: mr-disjoint, worktree isolation, PID-reuse and the ledger stay as they are.
alternatives.pros: Smallest possible diff (~10 lines across 2 files). Zero new mechanism to get wrong. Immediately removes the largest measured waste: 29 of 44 audits flagged, 10 of them with zero evidence, each costing one full-diff LLM read. Directly follows Google's static-analysis evidence — a detector at 100% effective-FP is removed, not tuned. Reversible by `git checkout` of two files. Fits one tiny slice, so it survives any credit-pressure state under D1.
alternatives.cons: Leaves the loop with NO mechanical pre-merge integrity signal at all, so the classes that actually escaped (vacuous-green gates, the concat!() scanner-dodge in production source, ceilings ratcheting upward) remain caught only by the LLM reviewer reading prose. Fixes none of the scheduling-correctness defects: two concurrent slices still collide on ARCHITECTURE.md + DIGEST.md by construction, a slice can still write to the main checkout, a recycled PID after reboot still masks a dead run forever, and the ledger SSOT is still gitignored with a 3-week-old backup. Excluding .codegraph outright also contradicts the reviewed decision recorded at mr-native-tick.sh:246-252, which deliberately keeps it as the last accidental backstop for human edits inside a worktree.
alternatives.quality_impact: Neutral-to-slightly-negative. Removes noise but removes the only mechanical pre-merge check with it, and leaves four correctness gaps that can silently corrupt scheduling and accounting.
alternatives.credit_impact: Best in class: ~10 lines of authoring, and it recovers roughly 29 full-diff supervisor reads per 44 merges immediately. Nothing else in this list pays back faster per credit spent.

alternatives.name: B. One shared correctness library — refactor all five scripts onto mr-lib
alternatives.sketch: Create memory/projects/mr-lib.py with the primitives every script re-implements badly: `alive(pid, since_utc)` (PID + start-time guard), `expand_touches(paths, adr)` (the brief's companion rules), `classify_diff(base, head)` (comment/import-stripped, per-file net counters), `ledger_append(row)` (schema-validated, explicit cost_status). Then rewrite mr-audit, mr-native-tick.sh, mr-disjoint, mr-spawn and mr-record to call it. One coherent module, one place to fix each class of bug.
alternatives.pros: Eliminates the real structural problem: the same predicate is written 3–4 times with divergent semantics (the PID check exists at mr-native-tick.sh:115, :151 and :178 in three shapes; comment-stripping exists in mr-audit and in 12 Rust test files). A single tested seam is the correct engineering answer and matches the repo's own proven `game-core` pure-seam pattern.
alternatives.cons: Big-bang refactor of the ONE part of this system that is measured to be working — the event bridge, flock and lock hygiene show 0 ORPHAN-RUN, 0 WATCHER-DEAD, 0 CRASHED in-window, and every one of those properties lives in the code this would rewrite. There is no test harness for the supervisor scripts at all, so the refactor would be verified only by running the live loop against real money. It is one indivisible large slice, which is exactly what D4's decomposition target exists to prevent, and a mid-refactor failure strands the whole loop rather than one slice.
alternatives.quality_impact: High ceiling, high variance. If it lands cleanly the supervisor layer becomes genuinely maintainable; if it half-lands it breaks lock hygiene, which is the load-bearing property.
alternatives.credit_impact: Worst in class. Large single slice, no incremental value until the last file is converted, and a failure mid-way costs a full re-do plus whatever the broken loop spends before it is noticed.

alternatives.name: C. Instrument-then-gate — convert each broken boolean tripwire into a measured predicate, ship every new check dry-run-first, and make the three structural gaps mechanical (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: Sequenced independent small slices. Kill the gating-test flag semantics outright (delete, not tune) and keep its counters as REPORTED magnitude; replace it with a narrow detector aimed only at fingerprints of defects that measurably escaped (concat!() scanner-dodge in production .rs; a numeric ceiling moving UP; a test/eval file with a NEGATIVE net assert delta), shipped in audit-only for one reset cycle before it may flag. Repoint CENSUS at the slice logs using mr-audit:28's already-correct parser. Make the human probe attribution-aware (tracked-and-clean ⇒ machine write) instead of path-blind, with a dry-run week logging old-vs-new verdict. Expand mr-disjoint by the brief's own companion rules before comparing, and add a RECONCILED class so the measured ARCHITECTURE.md+DIGEST.md collision becomes VISIBLE rather than absent. Move worktree creation from the LLM into mr-spawn so the slice's cwd is its worktree by construction. Add a start-time PID-reuse guard at all three sites. Add a daily backup + explicit cost_status + per-run log rotation.
alternatives.pros: Every step is independently shippable, independently falsifiable, and independently revertible — the shape D4 asks for. It applies the established rollout pattern from the research (Gatekeeper dryrun→warn→deny, Google's <10% effective-FP floor) rather than inventing one, so no new detector can repeat gating_test_audit's history. Each change replaces a boolean with a magnitude, which is the direct RF-1 remedy. The scheduling-correctness fixes (disjointness expansion, worktree cwd, PID guard) are pure correctness with no throughput implication — they make the loop strictly more conservative, never more parallel. Does not touch mr-audit:22-38, the STRUCTURAL always-serial list, the brief's TARGET_DESC block, or the reviewer/red-team gauntlet.
alternatives.cons: More total steps than A, so more supervisor attention across more ticks. The dry-run periods mean the probe and the new detector deliver no enforcement for a week or more. Two steps (worktree cwd, log rotation) change the launch contract and therefore carry real blast radius on the working parts.
alternatives.quality_impact: Strongly positive on the operator's PRIMARY axis. Turns four instruments that currently emit noise into instruments that emit numbers, closes two silent-corruption paths (PID reuse masking a dead run; main-checkout mutation by a live slice), and makes the fan-out safety check compare the set that actually exists rather than the declared subset.
alternatives.credit_impact: Net saving. Recovers ~29 full-diff supervisor reads per 44 merges (the same win as A) plus the collision-rework the disjointness expansion prevents (3 of ~20 merges hit doc conflicts), against an authoring cost spread over ~8 small slices that can each be deferred individually under D1.

alternatives.name: D. Push the gate into the repo — branch protection + a per-PR mutation leg, supervisor becomes merge-only
alternatives.sketch: Stop auditing diffs at the orchestration layer entirely. In the game repo: `gh api -X PUT` to require the `ci` and `e2e` status checks on master (currently HTTP 404 — master has NO protection at all), and add a per-PR `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <pr.diff> --annotations github` job with zero tolerated survivors in the diff. mr-audit's gating half is deleted; the supervisor merges only on a green required check.
alternatives.pros: This is the ESTABLISHED solution and the research says so plainly: cargo-mutants' own CI guidance recommends exactly a PR-diff leg, and it is the mechanically correct replacement for a lexical diff-shape check — it deletes the code the slice just wrote and demands a test notice, instead of guessing whether the diff 'looks tested'. It cannot be gamed by comment volume or line count, it catches the removable-security-guard class at the moment the guard is written, and it costs CI minutes rather than weekly plan credits — the asymmetry that matters most under the operator's secondary priority. Branch protection is one `gh api` call and is the single cheapest mechanical guard available anywhere in this backlog.
alternatives.cons: Solves exactly ONE of the seven items in this workstream. CENSUS, the human-activity probe, mr-disjoint, worktree isolation, reboot-path liveness and ledger integrity are all orchestration-layer concerns that no repo-side gate can reach. The cargo-mutants book is explicit that --in-diff is not a substitute for a full run and that the diff is matched only against code under test — a PR that guts a test file generates zero mutants and reads green, which is precisely the class this workstream is asked to catch. Also unmeasured cost: the per-PR leg's CI minutes on this repo have never been measured, and branch protection could deadlock the supervisor's own merge path if the required check names are wrong.
alternatives.quality_impact: High for the coverage question, zero for the other six defects.
alternatives.credit_impact: Excellent for the part it covers (CI minutes, not credits), but it leaves six defects unaddressed, so it cannot be the whole answer.

designs.chosen:
C — Instrument-then-gate, with D's branch-protection + `cargo mutants --in-diff` leg named as the explicit successor for the coverage question (not re-derived here, since it is a repo-side workstream).

The decisive reason is that the operator's PRIMARY priority is "the ability to test/debug/instrument/change each feature", and four of the seven items in this workstream are instruments that currently emit noise shaped like evidence — 159 of 162 CENSUS lines saying "agents: none" against a ground truth of 12 roles; 72 of 72 probe trips false; 29 of 44 audits flagged with 10 carrying zero mechanical evidence. A supervisor reading those instruments is worse off than one reading nothing, because it spends a full-diff read on each and learns nothing. Alternative A removes the noise but also removes the last mechanical pre-merge signal and leaves the two silent-corruption paths (PID reuse, main-checkout mutation) open. Alternative B is the right end state but is one indivisible large slice over the only code measured to be working, with no test harness, verified against live spend — the exact shape D4 exists to prevent. Alternative D is genuinely better than anything I would have invented for the coverage question and I defer to it there, but it reaches only one of seven items.

On value-per-credit, C and A recover the same headline win (~29 supervisor full-diff reads per 44 merges), but C additionally prevents the collision-rework that the disjointness defect causes — commit 45e08f2 is a full supervisor tick spent resolving a conflict on ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md that the current mr-disjoint reported as SAFE, because neither file is in its STRUCTURAL list nor derivable from declared touches. That rework is recurring and preventable, and preventing it costs one small slice.

One explicit disposition, since the task asks for it: gating_test_audit is DELETED, not retuned. Its measured effective-false-positive rate is 100% (11 in-window flags, 11 adjudicated CLEAN, 0 true positives across all 446 v3-era rows), an order of magnitude past the <10% floor at which Google's own programme removes a detector rather than tuning it — and their finding is that trust, once lost, is not recovered by tuning. Its counters survive as reported magnitude (the RF-1 remedy) so the supervisor keeps the data and loses the mandatory read. The replacement is deliberately NOT a better lexical scanner over the same question; it is a narrow set of fingerprints for defects that measurably escaped, shipped audit-only first, with the real coverage question handed to the repo-side mutation leg.

steps.title: PID-reuse guard on all three liveness checks
steps.files: /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-native-tick.sh:115 (reconcile part 2), :151 (decision-watch respawn), :178 (gate 1 LIVE)
steps.change: Add one shell helper near the top: `alive_since(){ pid=$1; since=$2; kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1; st=$(awk '{print $22}' /proc/$pid/stat 2>/dev/null) || return 1; bt=$(awk '/btime/{print $2}' /proc/stat); pstart=$(( bt + st / $(getconf CLK_TCK) )); [ "$pstart" -le "$(( since + 120 ))" ]; }` — the process must have started no later than ~2 minutes after the lock was written, which is impossible for a PID recycled after a reboot. Replace the bare `kill -0` at :115 with `alive_since "$PIDL" "$(started_epoch_from_lock)"`, at :178 likewise using the lock's started_utc, and at :151 using the decision-watch lock's own mtime. All values are confirmed available on this machine: /proc/stat btime=1785524423, /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, CLK_TCK=100.
steps.verification: Synthetic: write a lock with `session_leader: 1` (PID 1 started at boot) and `started_utc` set to now. Old code reports the run alive and never writes a CRASHED row; new code must report dead and the reconcile must emit the CRASHED row. FALSIFIED if it still reports alive. Negative control: a genuinely live mr-launch.sh leader must still report alive.
steps.risk: Clock skew or a lock whose started_utc is wrong could mark a live run dead, producing a spurious CRASHED ledger row — accounting noise, not a kill, since nothing in the reconcile signals a process. The 120s slack absorbs normal spawn latency (mr-spawn sleeps 4s then polls up to 90s before writing the lock, so the lock is written AFTER the process starts; the inequality direction is correct).
steps.rollback: Replace `alive_since "$p" "$s"` with `kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null` at the three sites.

steps.title: Ledger accuracy: explicit cost_status, and re-sum after a resume
steps.files: /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-record (ledger subcommand, cost handling); /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-native-tick.sh:50-56 (the `.recorded` short-circuit) and :82-83 (the FINISHED write)
steps.change: In mr-record, when --from-log yields no cost or mr-cost-sum returns '-', write `"cost_usd": null, "cost_status": "UNKNOWN"` explicitly instead of omitting the key — 710 rows currently carry cost_usd on only 653, so a missing key is indistinguishable from a genuine zero. Write `"cost_status": "OK"` on every successful sum. In the tick's reconcile, replace the unconditional `[ -e "$DF.recorded" ] && continue` at :52 with a re-sum trigger: continue only if the `.recorded` marker is NEWER than the pass log's mtime; otherwise re-run mr-cost-sum, and if the new total exceeds the recorded one, append a `CORRECTION(resume-delta)` row for the difference and re-touch the marker. This is the mechanism behind the $46.84 of measured missing spend: a resume pass appends to the same log after the FINISHED row is written, and today nothing ever re-reads it.
steps.verification: Reproduce it: take a merged slice's pass log, append a synthetic stream-json result event carrying a higher cumulative total_cost_usd, backdate the `.recorded` marker, and run the tick. FALSIFIED unless a CORRECTION row appears carrying exactly the delta and nothing else changes. Then re-run the reconcile over all existing .done files and confirm the recovered total is within a few dollars of the $46.84 figure — that number is the acceptance criterion.
steps.risk: A double-count if CORRECTION rows are themselves later summed. The reconcile's ALREADY check at :58-77 already skips rows whose outcome starts with CORRECTION (added 2026-08-01), so the exclusion path exists and must be preserved.
steps.rollback: Revert the two edits independently; cost_status is purely additive and the re-sum trigger reverts to the unconditional skip.

Building a better lexical scanner as the ANSWER to the gating question: deliberately refused. The research shows the established replacement is cargo-mutants' per-PR --in-diff leg plus branch protection, and I named that as the successor rather than re-deriving a scanner. A big-bang shared-library refactor (alternative B) of the code that is measured to be working (0 ORPHAN-RUN, 0 WATCHER-DEAD, 0 CRASHED in-window): rejected. It is one indivisible large slice over untested orchestration code verified only against live spend — precisely what D4's decomposition target exists to prevent.

designs.workstream: WS6 — Doctrine, planning pipeline, and the meta-process (RF-0). Scope: the supervisor instruction surface (`$MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md`, 155 lines, 24 dated incident parentheticals across 7 July dates, re-sent every tick and unchanged through a 183%-of-cap run, an overage trajectory, 11 false gate flags and ~21h of self-disable); the planning pipeline (spec elaboration is doctrinally interactive and structurally unlaunchable — `mr-spawn:16` hard-fails without `/tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.vars.json` and `mr-spawn:46` hard-fails without `tier`, neither of which a design sketch has); slice sizing at planning time (operator decision D4); the review cadence (13 residual milestones / 85 slices, output flat at 6-9 while cadence went 7d→6d→3d→4d, scoped exclusively to the game); the meta-process (every quality column in the ledger is dead — MEASURED: `remote_red_fix_cycles` sums 27.0 across all 710 rows and 0 across the 446 v3-era rows; `master_ci_after` is empty on 376/710 and reads `pending` on 20); and retiring dead ceremony (mr-feedback 15,911 B polled every tick at `mr-native-tick.sh:134` against a ledger frozen 2026-07-27, `mr-metrics` 6,935 B with 0 call sites, `mr-evidence` 746 B with 0 call sites, the N≥3 protocol at prompt L99 with 0 uses, the ollama triage hop at `mr-launch.sh:101` with 0 invocations across two generations).

alternatives.name: A1 — Prose-only refresh (minimal / do-nothing-plus)
alternatives.sketch: Edit files only, no new mechanism. Rewrite `$MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md` into a tighter document; delete doctrine line 81's self-disable clause; add `utilization` to the line-116 field list; move the 24 dated parentheticals into a referenced scars file; delete the feedback/retro prompt blocks (L31/L32/L34/L83/L105) and archive the dead scripts; add a written 'ceiling: 120 lines' maintenance rule and a written convergence rule to `mr-weekly-review-prompt.md`. One routine slice, no scripts written.
alternatives.pros: Cheapest thing that fixes the two named correctness bugs in the prompt (L81 self-arm of the operator-only kill switch; L116 telling the model to look at a field set that omits the one continuous gauge in the payload). Zero regression risk to the working machinery (brief construction, mutex/lock hygiene, mr-audit:22-38, the reviewer/red-team gauntlet are all untouched). Fits one tier cap with room; can be done under credit pressure. Archiving dead ceremony is signal-integrity work that stands on its own.
alternatives.cons: The mechanism that failed IS a prose rule with no consumer. The 24 scars are themselves prior prose fixes that did not hold; a 25th (the line ceiling) is the same move again, and a ceiling nothing measures is unenforceable by construction. Leaves `touches:` and `after:` with zero mechanical consumers, so 'nothing remains' stays a judgement call — which means deleting L81's self-disable clause has no safe replacement predicate. Leaves elaboration unlaunchable, sizing unestimated, and every process change unfalsifiable. The reviewed week already ran this experiment.
alternatives.quality_impact: Fixes two real correctness defects immediately; delivers nothing durable. Doctrine regrows on the next incident, at the observed rate of ~3.4 scars/week.
alternatives.credit_impact: ~1 routine slice (~$25-60), once. Leaves the measured rediscovery cost (13.1-day mean disclosure→remediation latency; the batch review re-deriving findings the in-slice reviewer already found) fully in place.

alternatives.name: A2 — Executable doctrine: every normative rule names a mechanical consumer or is tagged `judgment` (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: Invert the direction of enforcement. (1) `$MEM/mr-doctrine-lint` requires every `##` section of the supervisor prompt to carry `<!-- consumer: <script>|judgment|scars#<id> -->`, errors when a named consumer script does not exist (the dead-pointer detector — the mechanical version of 'ACTIVE v1.0' pointing at a ledger frozen for 19 days), and holds a monotone-shrinking line ceiling with a rot detector; its output rides `mr-situation`, which is read in-prompt every tick. (2) The prompt is then rewritten so each surviving line is either judgment or a pointer to its consumer; scars move to `$MEM/mr-doctrine-scars.md`. (3) `mr-ready` gives `touches:`/`after:` their first mechanical consumer and defines 'nothing remains'. (4) `mr-size` turns D4's decomposition target into a computed band, and a cap breach becomes an EVENT (headroom query), never a stop. (5) A `spec` tier plus an operator-owned allowlist file makes unattended elaboration a mechanical permission rather than a prose one. (6) `mr-record change` pre-registers each process change with a metric and a predicted direction; a re-pointed `mr-metrics` renders CONFIRMED/REFUTED/INCONCLUSIVE inside the existing weekly review.
alternatives.pros: Matches established practice on every axis the research supplies, and in two cases the repo has already independently reinvented it and proved it works: the monotone-shrinking exemption set with a rot detector exists at `scripts/adr-digest.mjs:55-96` (BACKLINK_ERA_MIN + KNOWN_BACKLINK_GAPS, 'THIS SET MAY ONLY SHRINK') and at `evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:121-160` (KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7, self-retiring, each entry owner-tagged) — this is Betterer's two-way `betterer ci` semantic, hand-rolled and green. Google's static-analysis result says the rule must live at the decision point, not on a universally-visible dashboard: an always-resent doctrine file IS the abandoned dashboard, and `mr-situation` is the decision point. Google's TODO rule (a tag must carry a tracked ID because 'bugs are tracked and have follow-up comments') is the precise diagnosis of `touches:`/`after:`/Residuals. Directly serves the operator's PRIMARY priority: every consumer is a standalone script with a proof-of-teeth, so the doctrine becomes testable and debuggable. Costs credits once and enforces free forever.
alternatives.cons: ~8-10 small loop-infra slices producing zero game value; under D1 credit pressure the whole programme defers. Every new script is a new thing that can rot (mitigated by the dead-pointer detector, which is the entire point, but the mitigation is itself new code). `mr-situation` grows and is read every tick. The lint can produce noise if it emits anything but failures.
alternatives.quality_impact: Converts the recurring failure class (rule disclosed, never enforced, rediscovered weeks later) into a mechanical one. Two measured under-tierings on security-adjacent work and the 4-of-21 cap breaches become computed, logged facts rather than judgement misses.
alternatives.credit_impact: Front-loaded: ~8-10 small slices spread over 3-4 weeks, deferrable individually under D1 because no step strands another. Recovers the rediscovery cost (estimated $50-150/week upper bound) and, via mr-ready, recovers CHOICE — 13r-a (CRITICAL) sat unlaunched at 2026-08-10T05:00:52Z while the tick logged 'no mechanical slice launchable' and the spec holding four `after: none` slices had been committed 5h earlier as 45b9b6d.

alternatives.name: A3 — Deterministic supervisor: move the decision into the wrapper
alternatives.sketch: Rewrite `mr-native-tick.sh` into a state machine that computes the action (merge / launch / resume / stand down) from live ground truth and only spawns an LLM to adjudicate a FLAGGED merge diff or to write prose. The doctrine file shrinks to a page of adjudication criteria because the procedure is code.
alternatives.pros: Maximal prose elimination; regrowth is structurally impossible; the tick becomes cheap and deterministic; the gate order becomes unit-testable.
alternatives.cons: Rejected. It re-litigates the one layer with no measured defect — 0 of 18 merges show scope re-derivation and the merge adjudication is exactly where judgement genuinely lives (the hard-tier FLAGGED read on 13r-h was a doc-comment substring false positive that a script would have had to escalate anyway). The build cost is very large under a fully-consumed weekly allowance, and a half-built state machine is the worst possible thing to strand under D1. It also concentrates blast radius: a wrapper bug now launches $60-400 runs unattended with no reviewer in the path, on a script that already carries five separately-documented near-miss fixes in its own comments (`:181` archive fastpath, `:190-194` watcher predicate, `:200-210` orphan-run age bound, `:262` injection hardening, `:324-327` the two-line CEN2 bug).
alternatives.quality_impact: Would improve determinism of the procedure and degrade the quality of the ambiguous cases, which are the cases that matter.
alternatives.credit_impact: Very high one-time cost, high risk of an expensive stranded rewrite; no credible recovery path within one allowance week.

alternatives.name: A4 — Operator cadence only: stop automating the meta-process
alternatives.sketch: Delete the automated improvement machinery. Generate one honest weekly one-pager; the operator reads it fortnightly and makes every loop change by hand. No lint, no registry, no pre-registration.
alternatives.pros: Highest signal integrity per unit of machinery — nothing can rot because nothing is claimed. Cheapest in credits. The one-pager is genuinely the highest-value artefact in the whole programme.
alternatives.cons: Violates D5 (reducing operator babysitting is itself a goal) and spends the scarcest resource in the system. The measured failure is not that the operator decided wrongly — it is that between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-15 nobody looked at all; making 'looking' a standing human obligation with no trigger and no artefact-with-teeth is the same failure with a calendar invite attached. Also leaves the planning starvation untouched: no amount of operator attention makes a design sketch launchable while `mr-spawn:16/:46` require a slice id and a tier.
alternatives.quality_impact: Good on the cases the operator reads; nothing on the cases that never surface.
alternatives.credit_impact: Near zero, and partially adopted — its one-pager is step WS6-10, wired into the EXISTING weekly review rather than shipped as a standalone ceremony (standalone maintenance ceremonies in this system are 0-for-3 on survival).

designs.chosen: A2 — Executable doctrine. Decisive reason, judged on the operator's PRIMARY priority first: a prose rule with no mechanical consumer is, by construction, a feature that cannot be tested, debugged, instrumented or safely changed — it is exactly the defect class the operator's primary priority names, sitting in the loop's own control plane. And the experiment separating A1 from A2 has already run: the reviewed week held 155 lines of doctrine and 24 dated scars (each one a prior prose fix), and produced a 182.9% cap breach, an overage-risk trajectory, 11 false gate flags with 0 true positives, and ~21h of supervisor self-disable, while changing not one line of the doctrine. Anything that keeps enforcement in prose is a re-run of that week. Second, on value-per-credit: a consumer script costs credits once and enforces free on every subsequent tick, whereas a prose rule is re-read roughly 500 times a week and enforces nothing; and the two highest-value single steps (mr-ready, which recovers CHOICE, and the ledger fields, which make everything else falsifiable) are each one small slice. Third, on risk: the pattern is not novel here — the repo has already built the exact ratchet twice (`scripts/adr-digest.mjs:55-96`, `evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:121-160`) and both are green and load-bearing, so this generalises a proven local template rather than importing an untested one. A3 is rejected because it attacks the one layer with no measured defect; A4 is rejected on D5 but its one-pager is adopted as WS6-10; A1 is subsumed — its two prompt bug-fixes are inside WS6-5 and its archiving is WS6-4, but its line-ceiling-as-prose is replaced by a ceiling with a consumer.

steps.title: Pre-registration: `mr-record change` + $MEM/mr-changes.jsonl
steps.files: /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-record (new `change` subcommand alongside `ledger`/`handoff` at the `if SUB==...` dispatch); new /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-changes.jsonl
steps.change: `mr-record change --id <slug> --hypothesis '<one sentence>' --metric <ledger-column|log-counter> --baseline <measured value> --predict <up|down|flat> --review_after <N merged slices>` appends one JSON row. DO-NOT-RETRY #7 — cutting the heavy elaboration ceremony on format-equivalence grounds. `mr-spec-brief-template.md` carries the full lens battery verbatim (planner → reviewer + red-team + /simplify → verifier); the only additions are the PR-never-merge terminal state and the OPEN DESIGN DECISIONS requirement.

The doctrine line ceiling is a one-way-down ratchet with a rot detector (the adr-digest.mjs:55-96 / scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:121-160 pattern), the size estimator is scored by prediction error (MAPE) rather than a ceiling, and WS6-10 reports mutation survival RATE per module, never the absolute survivor cap.

The elaboration slice is justified on turning a 9.2-hour attended session into an async PR review (D5), never in 'runway hours'.

designs.workstream: WS1 — Credit governance, pacing and cost truth for the Monster Realm autonomous build loop. Make the loop spend a weekly PLAN ALLOWANCE well without operator babysitting: persist the real account-wide gauge (rate_limit_info.seven_day.utilization), demote the synthetic internal-dollar model to relative attribution only (D2), pace via admission control rather than kills (D1/D3/D4), auto-re-arm at the weekly reset (D5), trip on overage, measure the harness's share of account utilization (MD-2), and stop the brief from asserting a mechanical ceiling that does not exist.

alternatives.name: A. Instrument-only (the do-nothing-plus / minimal option)
alternatives.sketch: Harvest every `type=="rate_limit_event"` object from harness stream-json logs into a durable JSONL under $MEM, reduce it to a per-week `util_floor` + `week_elapsed_frac` + `pace_ratio`, surface that inside mr-situation's JSON bundle (which the tick already pastes into the prompt at mr-native-tick.sh:291), and stop. No band, no gate, no hold file, no change to any launch path. The LLM supervisor sees the true number and exercises judgement.
alternatives.pros: Smallest possible diff and the lowest possible risk of a WRONG automatic hold — under this operator's economics an unnecessary idle hour forfeits allowance, which is a failure of the same kind as overage. Fixes RF-1 for this signal outright (magnitude preserved, not collapsed to a boolean). Cannot break anything on the WHAT IS WORKING list because it touches no launch, merge, lock or brief path. Produces exactly the pre-period a later gate needs (the Gatekeeper dryrun pattern from the research), so a gate built on top of it can be promoted on measured precision rather than hope.
alternatives.cons: It relies on an LLM reading a number in a prompt and acting on it — which is precisely the mechanism that already failed. The supervisor prompt ALREADY receives allowed_warning events carrying utilization on every tick and doctrine tells it to dismiss them (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md, 'Rate-limit watch': `allowed_warning` is routine). Adding the same number one layer closer changes nothing mechanical. It delivers no D1 admission control, no D5 auto-re-arm, and would not have stopped the measured 29→90% walk of 2026-08-06..10. It also leaves the two-actor kill-switch and the queue-placement bug untouched.
alternatives.quality_impact: Neutral-positive. No code paths that produce quality change. Removes a blind spot for human review.
alternatives.credit_impact: Near zero to run (harvest is file I/O in the existing tick; no model calls). Saves nothing by itself — it is measurement, not control.

alternatives.name: B. Cordon: admission-control pacing on a persisted plan-% gauge (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: Everything in A, plus: (1) a two-sided band over staleness-adjusted `util_floor` vs `week_elapsed_frac`, run in DRYRUN for one full reset cycle first; (2) an ADMISSION-CONTROL hold — a NEW file `$MEM/.native-supervisor-cordon`, deliberately NOT the existing `.native-supervisor-disabled` — that blocks the launch of NEW slices while leaving in-flight runs untouched and, critically, still spawning the tick whenever there is in-flight work or a queued done-event so the queue keeps draining; (3) auto-expiry keyed on the server-declared `resetsAt` in the gauge itself, so the cordon disarms itself at the weekly reset with zero operator action (D5); (4) an overage tripwire on `isUsingOverage`/`overageInUse`; (5) tier caps re-expressed as EMPIRICAL percentage-points-of-weekly-allowance measured from (slice, Δutilization) pairs, used as a decomposition target at planning time and a headroom query at run time (D4); (6) the internal-$ model kept but demoted to relative attribution, with its two 'pricing bugs' deliberately NOT fixed (see the measurement below).
alternatives.pros: This is not a bespoke policy — it is the established primitive, independently reinvented in three production systems the research found: `kubectl cordon` (mark unschedulable; running pods explicitly NOT evicted, distinct from `drain`), Jenkins `quietDown`/`cancelQuietDown` (starts no new builds, running jobs complete, separate disarm command), and AWS Budgets Actions (deny-NEW-provisioning SCP, running resources untouched, ambiguous cases routed to approval). D1 IS cordon. Inheriting the primitive brings four properties the loop currently lacks and that are each a measured defect here: the pause state is a DIFFERENT state from the stop state (fixes the two-actor kill switch by construction); the hold sits BELOW the event queue so a finished slice's done-event is never stranded (the measured 83.9h strand was a flag-PLACEMENT bug); the hold auto-expires rather than persisting past its cause; and arming and disarming are separate acts. The band is two-sided because the SRE error-budget literature is explicit that budget is meant to be SPENT and 100% is not the target — under 'idle hours are free', a one-sided ceiling alarm silently drives chronic underspend, which forfeits allowance for nothing.
alternatives.cons: More moving parts than A, and a mis-set band can idle the loop. Mitigated three ways: the dryrun period measures the would-have-fired rate against Google's <10% effective-false-positive floor before the gate can hold anything; the BEHIND band actively pushes work out rather than only restraining it; and the cordon never touches a running process, so its worst failure is deferred work, never destroyed work. It also depends on a staleness model — answered below by a measured monotonicity property rather than by a guess.
alternatives.quality_impact: Positive and specifically protective of the PRIMARY priority. Because it defers rather than demotes (D3) and never kills (DO-NOT-RETRY #1), the review/red-team gauntlet and the tester lens are untouched at every band. Re-expressing caps in plan-% removes the only current pressure toward shrinking a slice below its honest size.
alternatives.credit_impact: Costs ~nothing to run: harvesting is file I/O inside a tick that already spawns, and the design deliberately requires NO paid probe (see D, rejected). Upside is bounded but real — the specific loss it prevents is overage, and purchased credits are the operator's stated true waste. Also converts the currently-dead 17 WARN / 11 STOP-MONITOR / 4 HARD-MONITOR signals into tier-cap calibration data.

alternatives.name: C. Replace the internal-$ model outright — plan-% becomes the only cost concept
alternatives.sketch: Take D2 literally and maximally: delete mr-cost-sum/mr-cost-watch/mr-budget-config's absolute limits and the ledger's cost column, and let `seven_day.utilization` be the single source of truth for everything cost-related.
alternatives.pros: One SSOT, no dual-truth confusion, and it immediately kills a model measured to be 1.60x wrong right now (internal governor 35.6% vs a real 57%). Conceptually the cleanest reading of D2.
alternatives.cons: Refuted by measurement. Plan-% is ACCOUNT-WIDE and carries no attribution: it cannot say which slice cost what, cannot price a tier cap, cannot detect a runaway single run, and cannot compute MD-2 (the harness's share) — the research is explicit that the local ledger is the ONLY possible attribution signal, and MD-2 is precisely the quantity every benefit estimate depends on. Worse, it removes the only LIVE signal: I measured that mr-cost-sum returns `-` (COST-UNKNOWN) for the entire duration of a run — /tmp/mr_pass_11r-g.log carries exactly ONE `"type":"result"` event, at the very end, so mr-cost-sum on 10/25/50/75/90% prefixes all return `-`. Token repricing exists because there is no alternative mid-run. D2 says demote to relative attribution; it does not say delete.
alternatives.quality_impact: Negative. Losing per-slice attribution removes the feedback that lets tier caps be sized honestly, which pushes back toward guessed caps and mis-sized slices.
alternatives.credit_impact: Neutral to negative — blinds the loop to single-run runaways between weekly samples.

alternatives.name: D. Paid idle-hour probe sampler
alternatives.sketch: Cron a minimal `claude -p` call every hour purely to elicit a fresh `rate_limit_event` during hours when the loop is idle, eliminating the staleness blind spot.
alternatives.pros: Removes the only genuine gap in the gauge — no sample exists when nothing is running.
alternatives.cons: Spends credits to measure credits, and it is unnecessary given two measured facts. First, seven_day utilization is monotone non-decreasing within a `resetsAt` bucket: across 255 samples in 3 week-buckets, the only within-file decreases are 4 instances of exactly 0.01 (quantisation dither at a rounding boundary, e.g. [0.95,0.96,0.95,0.96]), so `max()` over the bucket is a valid, dither-immune LOWER BOUND on current utilization and a stale sample is never dangerously optimistic. Second, the resume decision needs no measurement at all: `resetsAt` is carried in the sample itself, so auto-re-arm at the weekly reset is a TIMER, not a probe. The residual blind case — loop idle while the operator burns credits elsewhere — is handled by treating the stored max as a floor and widening the safety margin with sample age.
alternatives.quality_impact: None.
alternatives.credit_impact: Negative by construction. Keep as a named escalation only if the dryrun period shows the staleness margin actually costing launches.

alternatives.name: E. Fix the two measured pricing bugs (explicitly considered and REFUTED on measurement)
alternatives.sketch: In mr-cost-watch's `price_log` (lines 16-43) dedup usage events by `message.id`, and price `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` at the `cache_write_1h` rate the config already defines but never uses. Mirror in mr-usage-snap:24-28.
alternatives.pros: Both bugs are real and I reproduced both. In /tmp/mr_pass_13r-b.log there are 522 usage-bearing lines against 359 distinct `message.id` (1.454 events per message; histogram 247×1, 71×2, 31×3, 10×4). And a real usage block reads `"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":27834}` while both mr-cost-watch:39 and mr-usage-snap:28 charge the whole `cache_creation_input_tokens` at the 5m rate (opus 6.25 vs 10 per Mtok — a 1.6x under-price on that component).
alternatives.cons: Fixing them makes the estimator WORSE for its only purpose. Priced against the authoritative ledger (mr-cost-sum, which reads the CLI's own `total_cost_usd`) over 14 real runs totalling $786.99: current buggy code = mean 1.238x ledger (median 1.249, range 0.997–1.464) — biased HIGH, so a cap fires EARLY, the safe direction; dedup alone = mean 0.689x — undercounts by 31%; dedup + 1h-split = mean 0.717x — still 28% low, so a cap would fire LATE, the unsafe direction. The two errors are compensating, and the existing `costwatch_stream_factor: 0.8` is already the correct calibration (measured 1/1.238 = 0.808). The honest conclusion is that this is an uncalibrated heuristic that happens to be biased in the safe direction, and the correct action is to PIN and DOCUMENT the calibration, not to 'fix' it toward a different wrong answer.
alternatives.quality_impact: Negative — silently converts a conservative live estimator into an optimistic one on the one path that watches a running slice.
alternatives.credit_impact: Negative — a 28%-low live estimate raises the chance a runaway run is noticed late.

designs.chosen:
B — Cordon: admission control on a persisted plan-% gauge, rolled out dryrun-first.

The decisive reason, judged against the PRIMARY priority first: cordon is the only option that paces the loop WITHOUT ever touching the quality machinery. It defers admission of new work and leaves every running process, every review lens, every tier and every effort setting alone — so D3 ("never demote under credit pressure") is satisfied structurally rather than by policy, and DO-NOT-RETRY #1 (kills strand locks and merely REALLOCATE spend under a consumed allowance) is avoided by construction. A is honest but inert: the loop ALREADY receives utilization in the prompt on every tick and doctrine tells it to dismiss the event, so adding the number one layer closer changes nothing mechanical, delivers no D5 auto-re-arm, and would not have stopped the measured 29→90% walk. C is refuted by measurement — mr-cost-sum returns `-` for a run's entire lifetime (one result event per pass log), so deleting the token model blinds the only live signal, and it destroys the attribution needed for MD-2. D spends credits to learn something monotonicity already gives free.

Second reason, on value-per-credit: cordon is nearly free to build and free to run. The harvest is file I/O inside a tick that already spawns; the week identity is server-declared (`resetsAt`, observed as exactly 1786060800 / 1786665600 / 1787270400 — spaced 604800s, and 1786060800 − 1784851200 = exactly two weeks, independently confirming the existing anchor is phase-correct and must not be "fixed"); and the resume trigger is a timer, not a measurement. The concrete loss it prevents is overage, which the operator names as the true waste.

Third, it is not invented here. The research found the primitive independently reinvented three times in production (kubectl cordon, Jenkins quietDown, AWS Budgets deny-new-provisioning), and the operator's D1 is already a verbatim restatement of it. Adopting the established shape brings the four properties the loop measurably lacks: a pause state distinct from a stop state, a hold placed BELOW the queue, auto-expiry, and separate arm/disarm. Two of those are direct fixes for measured defects (the two-actor `.native-supervisor-disabled` ambiguity, and the 83.9h stranded done-event, which was a flag-PLACEMENT bug, not a policy bug).

Live state right now makes the case concrete and urgent: the week is 29.7% elapsed with `util_floor` = 0.57 (60 samples, week ends 2026-08-20 20:00 EDT) — a pace ratio of 1.92 — while the internal governor's last recorded reading was NORMAL at 35.6%, a 1.60x under-report, worse than the historical 1.39x. The freshest sample is 11.8h old and sits in /tmp, which is exactly the ephemerality the harvest fixes.

steps.title: Reduce the store to a plan-usage view and surface it — DRYRUN, no gate
steps.files: NEW $MEM/mr-plan-usage (python3, ~90 lines, or a `--report` mode of S1's script); EDIT mr-situation:126-131 (add `out["plan_usage"]` via the existing `safe()` wrapper, immediately after `out["budget"]=b`); EDIT mr-native-tick.sh:280-284 (read the band alongside GSTATE and log it — log ONLY, no branch)
steps.change: Emit `{week_resets_at, week_elapsed_frac, util_floor, util_samples, newest_sample_age_s, stale, pace_ratio, forecast_eow, forecast_sample_n, overage{...}, band, would_hold}`. Definitions, each grounded in a measured property: `util_floor` = max(utilization) over rows whose `resets_at` equals the CURRENT week's — valid because utilization is monotone non-decreasing within a bucket up to ±0.01 dither (measured: 4 decreases across 95 files, every one exactly 0.01), so max() is both dither-immune and a genuine lower bound on the present value. A `status=="rejected"` row in the current week contributes `util_floor = 1.0` in the DERIVED view only, never as a fabricated value in the raw store. STALENESS-ADJUSTMENT is one line and needs no decay model: because the stored value is a floor, staleness can only make the true value HIGHER, so the band compares `util_floor` against the band edge and additionally reports `stale=true` when `newest_sample_age_s` exceeds ~2 tick intervals, which widens the margin required to enter the BEHIND band (never the HOLD band). Week identity comes from the server-declared `resets_at`, with $MEM/.weekly-reset-anchor as fallback ONLY — the anchor is measurably correct (1786060800 − 1784851200 = exactly 2 weeks) and is not modified. Bands are TWO-SIDED: BEHIND (`pace_ratio` < ~0.8 → start work; unused allowance is forfeited, not saved), ON-PACE, AHEAD (advisory), HOLD (util_floor at/over the ceiling OR forecast_eow > 1.0), OVERAGE (S6). `forecast_eow` uses the slope of the last ≤48h of samples, falls back to the whole-week average below 2 samples, is clamped, and always reports `forecast_sample_n` so a one-sample 'forecast' is visibly untrustworthy. This step arms NOTHING — it only logs `PLAN-USAGE band=X would_hold=Y util_floor=Z elapsed=W` once per tick. That is the Gatekeeper `enforcementAction: dryrun` stage, and it produces the precision baseline S7 needs.

steps.title: Arm the cordon — admission control with auto-expiry (MUST BE ONE SLICE)
steps.files: NEW $MEM/.native-supervisor-cordon (JSON: `{armed_utc, armed_by, band, util_floor, week_resets_at, expires_at, reason}`); NEW $MEM/mr-cordon (arm|disarm|status, ~50 lines); EDIT mr-native-tick.sh — a ~12-line block inserted at line 211, immediately AFTER gate 1 has computed LIVE / DONE_WAIT / PENDING and BEFORE its `STANDDOWN live-chain` exit; EDIT mr-native-tick.sh:291 (prompt assembly) to render an ADMISSION-CLOSED constraint when cordoned
steps.change: Semantics, exactly cordon: (a) if the cordon file exists AND its `week_resets_at` differs from the current sample's `resets_at`, DELETE it and proceed — that single comparison is the whole of D5's automatic re-arm at the weekly reset, and it requires no operator action and no new sample, because `resetsAt` travels inside the gauge; a `expires_at` max-age is the belt-and-braces second disarm. (b) if cordoned AND (LIVE==1 OR DONE_WAIT==1 OR PENDING non-empty) → SPAWN the tick as normal but export the cordon state into the prompt as a hard constraint: merge, record, reconcile and finish in-flight work; launch NOTHING new. This is D1 verbatim ('finish in-flight work, start nothing new') and it is what keeps the queue draining. (c) if cordoned AND none of those → `log "STANDDOWN cordon (admission closed, nothing in flight)"; exit 0` — free, no model call. The placement at line 211 is the load-bearing detail and the direct fix for the measured 83.9h stranded done-event: the cordon sits BELOW the event queue, so unlike `.native-supervisor-disabled` at gate -1 (line 124) it can never hold a finished slice's done-event hostage. It is a DIFFERENT FILE from `.native-supervisor-disabled` on purpose — cordon is not drain, quietDown is not safeExit — which also makes the self-armed pace hold distinguishable from an operator stop without touching the kill switch's own semantics (that ambiguity is a real defect but belongs to another workstream; this step only refuses to make it worse). Arming is driven by the S2 band and is written by `mr-cordon arm`, never by a bare `touch`. This step MUST be one slice: a half-cordon that exits at the top of the tick reintroduces the exact stranded-event bug the placement exists to fix, and a cordon without auto-expiry reintroduces the indefinite-hold bug — the three pieces (placement, admission semantics, expiry) are one invariant and cannot be safely split.
steps.verification: Behavioural, before arming: with the cordon file hand-written and a fake live lock present, the tick must SPAWN (assert a `SPAWN` line in mr-native-tick.log); with the cordon present and no lock/done/pending, it must exit 0 with `STANDDOWN cordon` and NO spawn (assert cost 0 for that tick in the ledger). With the cordon's `week_resets_at` set to a previous week, the tick must DELETE it and proceed. Falsification at 30 days: zero occurrences of a done-event sitting unprocessed for more than one tick interval while cordoned; and zero weeks ending with `util_floor` < 0.6 attributable to a cordon that held while work was ready (that would be forfeited allowance — the failure mode this design is most at risk of).
steps.risk: A cordon armed on a wrong band idles the loop and forfeits allowance. Three guards: it cannot arm until the S2 dryrun period shows a would-hold false-positive rate under 10%; the BEHIND band actively pushes work out; and the worst outcome is deferred work, never destroyed work, because no running process is signalled. Second risk: interaction with the existing HARD-STOP gate at line 284 — leave that gate exactly as-is in this step so there is only one new decision point.
steps.rollback: `rm $MEM/.native-supervisor-cordon` disarms instantly and the loop resumes on the next tick; removing the 12-line block restores the previous control flow exactly. Both are single actions with no state to unwind.

steps.files: NEW $MEM/mr-harness-share (python3, ~70 lines, read-only); reads $MEM/mr-ratelimit.jsonl + $MEM/monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE RESULT to encode so it is not re-attempted: the 85h halt (2026-08-10T13:00Z → 08-14T01:52Z) is NOT usable as a natural experiment, for two independent reasons — no sessions ran, so no samples were emitted during it, and its endpoints straddle the weekly reset (0.90 in bucket 1786665600, resuming into bucket 1787270400), so the counter reset in between.
