antipatterns_avoided: DO-NOT-RETRY #1 — arming costwatch_enforce as a KILL. `costwatch_enforce` stays FALSE in every step. The cordon is COOPERATIVE and ADMISSION-ONLY: it never signals a running process, never touches a lock, never terminates a claude child. S0 goes further and corrects the brief's claim that a mechanical 125% ceiling exists, so the loop stops advertising a kill it does not have.

DO-NOT-RETRY #3 — raising duty cycle, N_MAX or cron frequency. Nothing here changes N, the hourly cron, or concurrency. The cordon only ever REDUCES admission, and the BEHIND band pushes existing queued work out rather than opening new slots.

DO-NOT-RETRY #13 — 'correcting' .weekly-reset-anchor. The anchor is not modified. It is independently confirmed correct (1786060800 − 1784851200 = exactly 2 weeks) and is demoted to a fallback behind the server-declared `resetsAt`, which is strictly better and requires no edit.

DO-NOT-RETRY #4 (by analogy) — an absolute cap that misreads growth as regression. Tier caps become empirical percentage-points with a reported n, and the relaunch block becomes a headroom query rather than a fixed ceiling, so a legitimately large slice is deferred by account headroom rather than blocked by an arbitrary number.

Tripping on `allowed_warning`. The single most dangerous naive move here, since it would park the loop for days over a routine notice — the exact outage the arming code's own comment (mr-native-tick.sh:353-356) exists to prevent. S3 is additive-only and the trip rule is preserved verbatim, with a hard revert trigger if any new ARMED line appears.

'Fixing' the two pricing bugs. Measured refutation over 14 runs / $786.99: current = 1.238x ledger (safe, fires early); dedup = 0.689x; dedup+1h = 0.717x (unsafe, fires late). S9 pins the calibration and records the counterfactual numbers instead, so the next agent cannot re-propose it from first principles.

Deleting the internal-$ model in the name of D2. Refuted by measurement — mr-cost-sum returns `-` for a run's whole lifetime (one result event per pass log), so it cannot serve as a live signal, and plan-% carries no attribution, which would make MD-2 uncomputable. D2 says demote to relative attribution; S10 demotes rather than deletes, and only after the replacement has survived a cycle.

Reusing `.native-supervisor-disabled` for the pace hold. That flag is already written by two indistinguishable actors; overloading it with a third meaning would deepen a known defect. The cordon is a separate file with structured provenance and its own arm/disarm commands, following cordon-vs-drain and quietDown-vs-safeExit.

Placing the hold above the event queue. The measured 83.9h stranded done-event was a flag-PLACEMENT bug. The cordon is inserted at mr-native-tick.sh:211, after gate 1 has computed LIVE/DONE_WAIT/PENDING, so a cordoned tick still spawns to drain the queue whenever work is in flight.

A one-sided ceiling alarm. Under 'idle hours are free, optimise value per weekly credit', forfeited allowance is a failure of the same kind as overage. The band is two-sided, with an explicit BEHIND state that tells the loop to start work.
A paid idle-hour probe. Rejected because monotonicity makes a stale sample a valid floor and `resetsAt` makes the re-arm a timer — spending credits to measure credits was avoidable.

Demoting model or effort tier under credit pressure (D3). No step touches SUP_MODEL, SUP_EFFORT, the tier block at mr-spawn:46-48, or the escalation path at mr-launch.sh:109-117. Pressure produces deferral only.

Shipping an unvalidated gate straight to enforcing. S2 runs the band in dryrun for a full reset cycle and S7 cannot arm until the would-hold false-positive rate clears the <10% effective-FP floor — the discipline whose absence produced gating_test_audit's 0-for-446 record.

Trimming the brief or the supervisor prompt for tokens (DO-NOT-RETRY #2). S0 is a same-length correction of a false statement; S3 is two lines added for correctness. TARGET_DESC, the touches: block, the tier block and the DoD are untouched.

Fabricating a value the API did not send. `utilization` is absent on `rejected` and `allowed` events (measured 118/118 and 2/2); the raw store records null. The 1.0 floor for a rejection lives only in the derived view, keeping raw and derived cleanly separated.

designs.workstream:
WS5 — Build-session context and token efficiency (RF-4). Measured baseline from 14 real build logs (/tmp/mr_pass_13r-{a..h}.log, 14r-{a,b,c,d,e,g}.log): 1,566M total prompt tokens; parent 722.0M (3,611 turns, mean 200K/turn) vs SUBAGENT 844.2M (7,696 turns, mean 110K/turn) — subagents are 54% of all prompt volume, not a minority. Cache hit rate 96.2%; input-cost mix cache_read 67.2% / cache_write 32.6% / fresh 0.1%. Parent context is strictly monotone in 13 of 14 sessions (endCtx == maxCtx), high-water 191K–465K, p50 200K. Preamble measured by live probe at 51,542 tokens = 24.0% of parent volume and 43.8% of subagent volume.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, all measured:
(1) The open question is ANSWERED and the stated cause is REFUTED. `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore` IS in the build session's tool list and the server reports status "connected" (system/init event, mr_pass_13r-e.log; also pre-approved at projects/monster-realm/.claude/settings.json:15 and registered user-scope in ~/.claude.json). MCP scope is not the cause. What IS measured: `Grep` and `Glob` are NOT in the eager tool list in ANY session (13r-e, 13r-d, 14r-g, and a live probe) — they are deferred behind ToolSearch, which is why the parent census shows Bash-heavy navigation. The per-session census is also far more varied than "Grep 0 / Glob 0 / codegraph 0": 13r-e alone shows Grep 164 / Glob 18 / codegraph 3. So this is inconsistent routing plus a tool-availability artefact, not a hard capability gap.
(2) "65% of build spend is prefix replay" is true as a VOLUME statement but overstates cost ~10x: 96.2% of that volume is cache_read, billed at ~0.1x. Preamble trimming is therefore worth far less than its token share; the expensive line item is cache_CREATION (32.6% of input cost from 3.7% of tokens), and 81–82% of cache-creation is SUBAGENT, not parent.
(3) The toolchain preamble is 29 distinct spellings, not two: 1,018 of 3,279 Bash calls (31.0%) carry an inline `export PATH=`, seven hardcode `nodejs/24.13.1`, and 7 calls reference `$HOME/.nvm/...` (incl. a v22.14.0) — a path that does NOT exist on this machine (`ls ~/.nvm` → No such file or directory). That is a live correctness bug masked by shim fallback, exactly the trap class the operator was already bitten by.

alternatives.name: A — Minimal: config hygiene only (the do-nothing-plus baseline)
alternatives.sketch: Change no control flow. (i) Add `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config $MEM/mr-build-mcp.json` to the two `claude` invocations in mr-launch.sh, exposing only codegraph + codebase-memory-mcp + spacetimedb-docs. (ii) Add a pinned toolchain env file sourced by one `just` recipe and referenced by one brief line. (iii) Add one brief line routing navigation through codegraph and naming Grep/Glob as ToolSearch-deferred. Leave session length, compaction and subagent scoping untouched.
alternatives.pros: Zero risk to the pre-code gauntlet, to touches: discipline, or to the brief. Every change is reversible by deleting a flag. (ii) is a genuine correctness fix with measured evidence (the nonexistent .nvm path). MCP scoping also removes 4 servers that are failed/needs-auth/pending at init (Indeed failed, Audible+ZipRecruiter needs-auth, 3 gitmcp pending), making startup deterministic and eliminating mid-session tool-list mutation as a cache-invalidation source. Implementable in under a day.
alternatives.cons: The measured savings are small and I verified this rather than assuming it: a live A/B probe showed the eager tool list drop 105 → 26 tools but total preamble only 51,542 → 48,437 tokens (−3,105, −6%). Tool DEFERRAL is already suppressing most schema cost, so my own 'consumer MCP crowding' hypothesis is largely refuted — 79 fewer tools bought ~40 tokens each, not ~250. Across the corpus that is ~35M of 1,566M tokens ≈ 2.2% of volume, and at 96% cache-hit the dollar effect is smaller still. The PATH fix saves ~25K tokens total — negligible as a token play. Leaves the dominant lever (monotone context growth) completely untouched.
alternatives.credit_impact: MEASURED −2.2% of prompt volume, ~−1% of input cost. Effectively a rounding error against the weekly allowance.
alternatives.quality_impact: Mildly positive. Deterministic toolchain removes a real (if currently latent) failure mode; deterministic MCP set removes startup nondeterminism.

alternatives.name: B — CLI autocompact ceiling (the established, vendor-supplied solution)
alternatives.sketch: Add `--autocompact 250000` to the parent `claude` invocations in mr-launch.sh:85 and :124. The CLI ships this natively (`--autocompact <auto|tokens>`, 100k–1M) — I verified the flag exists in the installed CLI 2.1.233. Move the non-negotiable scope contract (slice id, touches: set, forbidden commands, valid stopping points) into `--append-system-prompt` so a compaction pass cannot erase it.
alternatives.pros: This is the OFFICIAL mechanism for exactly this problem and it is one flag. Per the research method rule I compared my own design against it honestly. It directly closes the named gap (0 compaction events across 231 transcripts, one session at 611K with no backstop). It needs no new scripts, no new flags, no session-side cooperation, and no change to the brief's body. It also caps the tail risk that motivated the finding in the first place.
alternatives.cons: Measured counterfactual is modest and is an UPPER BOUND: clipping every parent+subagent turn at 250K saves 108.4M of 1,566M = 6.9%; at 200K, 13.6%; at 300K, only 3.1%. Real compaction is strictly worse than clipping because the summary is written at the 1.25x cache-creation rate and dropped files get re-read. The decisive objection is on the PRIMARY axis: compaction summarises the conversation, and the single most valuable measured property of this loop is that the brief holds — zero of 18 merges show scope re-derivation. A compaction that paraphrases the touches: set or the valid-stopping-points list attacks precisely that. `--append-system-prompt` mitigates but does not eliminate this, and it cannot protect the mid-session state (which phase the gauntlet is in, which EARS criteria are already covered). Compaction is also blind to phase structure — it can fire in the middle of a tester's red-first pass.
alternatives.credit_impact: MEASURED upper bound −6.9% of volume at C=250K; realistic −3 to −5% after the summarisation write-back. Roughly 2-3x approach A.
alternatives.quality_impact: Net risk, not net gain. Unbounded windows do carry a real tail hazard, but the mechanism trades a rare failure for a continuous, unattributable erosion of the one thing that measurably works.

alternatives.name: C — Cooperative context-budget segmentation at phase boundaries (CHOSEN)
alternatives.sketch: Treat context like the credit allowance: gauge it, arm a cooperative cordon, cut at a SAFE point, resume fresh. (1) mr-cost-watch — which already tails /tmp/mr_pass_$S.log and parses usage JSON — additionally computes parent context per turn (input + cache_read + cache_creation on assistant events with parent_tool_use_id == null) and records the running max. (2) When it crosses a threshold it writes `/tmp/mr_seg_<slice>`, semantically 'checkpoint at your NEXT phase boundary; you WILL be relaunched'. (3) One brief line adds that flag to the poll list the brief already teaches at every phase boundary (template line 13). (4) mr-launch.sh, on a clean exit with the segment flag set, relaunches FRESH — a new `claude -p` with the same brief and RESUME_BLOCK populated from the progress memo — instead of `--resume`, which restores the transcript and so does not reset context at all.
alternatives.pros: Largest measured effect by a wide margin. Modelling each session as 2 equal segments against its real per-turn context series: parent 722.0M → 378.4M = −47.6% (ideal, zero re-orientation). Measured re-orientation cost is only 12.1% of parent volume (pre-first-edit), and a resumed segment pays less because the progress memo names the exact next step — so net ≈ −35% of parent volume ≈ −16% of ALL prompt volume, versus 6.9% UPPER BOUND for autocompact. It also cuts at DECLARED PHASE BOUNDARIES rather than a token count, so the gauntlet is never interrupted mid-lens — this is the research finding's explicit recommendation (segment at completed sub-goals with a written handoff, never at a fixed turn count). Almost all machinery already exists and is proven: the checkpoint prompt (mr-launch.sh:138) already commits WIP, pushes and writes the handoff; the progress-memo format is already mandated and already produced; RESUME_BLOCK already exists (mr-spawn:49, template line 9); the flag-polling contract already exists and works. It is a cooperative stop-flag — the one enforcement shape DO-NOT-RETRY #1 explicitly permits. And the gauge fixes RF-1 in the same stroke: a continuous number is recorded, not a bit.
alternatives.cons: Most moving parts of the three, and the one that can strand work if built wrong. Segment 2 could re-orient badly if the progress memo is thin, turning a saving into a loss. Requires a measured, non-negotiable dependency order (gauge in MONITOR before any flag is armed) and one atomic slice that cannot be split. `--resume` does not reset context is INFERRED from 14r-e reaching 334K across multiple attempts rather than resetting per attempt — cheap to falsify and the design must be verified against it first. Marginal returns fall off fast: 3 segments buys only 6.7 points over 2 (−54.3% vs −47.6%), so more aggressive segmentation is not worth the added park risk.
alternatives.credit_impact: MEASURED ideal −47.6% of parent volume; realistic −30 to −38% of parent ≈ −14 to −17% of ALL prompt volume. CONTINGENT on re-orientation staying near the measured 12.1%.
alternatives.quality_impact: Neutral-to-positive if and only if cuts land at phase boundaries. A fresh segment starting at ~52K instead of 400K is operating far from the degraded-attention region, and the brief is re-sent verbatim rather than summarised — so unlike (B) it strengthens rather than erodes the property that scope is never re-derived.

alternatives.name: D — Attack the subagent layer directly (largest single line item; rejected as the PRIMARY move)
alternatives.sketch: Subagents are 844.2M of 1,566M tokens (54%). Measured breakdown by role across 14 sessions: tester 295.7M (35.0% of subagent volume, 20 runs, 77.9 turns/run) · reviewer 189.1M (22.4%, 30 runs) · red-team 138.4M (16.4%, 24 runs) · general-purpose 56.1M (6.6%) · planner 55.2M (6.5%) · verifier 53.5M (6.3%). Cut subagent cost by capping fan-out, shortening lens runs, or consolidating roles.
alternatives.pros: It is the biggest number on the board and the brief correctly identifies tester as the right target within it — my measurement confirms the direction (35% of subagent volume, 77.9 turns/run mean).
alternatives.cons: Reviewer + red-team + verifier are 45.1% of subagent volume and are exactly the pre-code gauntlet that is MEASURED to be the best-spending part of the loop (93 runs, ~$171/wk, found a merge blocker before code existed and a HIGH after CI was green). Any general subagent-cost programme lands on them. Tester alone is safe to target but the tester lens is core DoD and mandatory on every non-doc slice — a missing tester invocation mechanically forces an extra paid review pass, so cutting it can INCREASE spend. That leaves only scoping improvements (give tester the plan-file path and the exact test-file paths instead of a re-inlined narrative), which is real but small: the re-inlined narrative traffic is ~592K tokens against 844M — 0.07%. The saving would have to come from fewer orientation TURNS, which is contingent and unmeasured.
alternatives.credit_impact: Unquantifiable up front, and negative in the plausible failure mode where a thinned lens causes rework.
alternatives.quality_impact: Directly threatens the WHAT IS WORKING list. Rejected as a headline approach; the safe, narrow slice of it (tester input scoping only, never tester removal or model demotion) is retained as step S7.

designs.chosen:
C — cooperative context-budget segmentation at phase boundaries, with A folded in as cheap prerequisite hygiene and the narrow safe slice of D as a trailing step.

The decisive reason is that C is the only option that scores on the PRIMARY axis and the SECONDARY axis in the same mechanism, and I chose it over the established vendor solution (B) on measured evidence rather than preference.

PRIMARY first. The operator's priority is code quality and the ability to test/debug/change each feature, and the loop's single most valuable measured property is that the brief holds — zero of 18 merges show scope re-derivation. B (`--autocompact`) is the official mechanism and I would normally defer to it, but it works by summarising the conversation, and the conversation is where the touches: set, the valid-stopping-points list and the current gauntlet phase live. It is also phase-blind: it can fire mid-tester, mid-red-team. C re-sends the brief VERBATIM at each segment and cuts only at boundaries the brief already declares safe (after the plan + ADRs; after tests are written; after each green increment). A segment that begins at ~52K instead of ending at 465K is also operating far from the degraded-attention region — so C plausibly improves the quality of late-slice work, where B degrades it. C additionally repairs RF-1 at its source: mr-cost-watch starts recording a continuous context gauge instead of discarding magnitude, which is the same defect that threw away the utilization number.

SECONDARY second. Measured, not asserted: modelling two segments against each session's real per-turn context series gives parent 722.0M → 378.4M (−47.6% ideal), and the measured re-orientation cost is only 12.1% of parent volume — so net ≈ −35% of parent ≈ −16% of ALL prompt volume. B's counterfactual is 6.9% and that is an UPPER BOUND that real compaction cannot reach, because the summary is written at the 1.25x cache-creation rate. C is worth roughly 2.5x B on the axis B was chosen for, while being the safer of the two on the axis that actually binds.

Two facts made this affordable rather than speculative. First, almost every part already exists and is proven in production: the checkpoint prompt at mr-launch.sh:138 already commits WIP, pushes and writes the handoff; the progress-memo format is already mandated (template line 13) and already on disk; RESUME_BLOCK already exists (mr-spawn:49); the flag-poll contract already works. The genuinely new code is a ~15-line gauge inside a script that already tails the same log and already writes flags. Second, C is a cooperative stop — the one enforcement shape the DO-NOT-RETRY list explicitly permits — so it never kills, never strands a lock, never demotes a model or effort tier, and under credit pressure it defers rather than degrades (D1/D3 hold by construction).

I did NOT choose D despite it being the largest line item, because reviewer + red-team + verifier are 45.1% of subagent volume and are the protected gauntlet, and because a missing tester invocation mechanically triggers an extra paid review pass — cutting there can raise spend. Only the input-scoping slice of D survives, as S7.

steps.title: Context GAUGE in mr-cost-watch — MONITOR only, no action (the RF-1 fix and the dryrun period)
steps.files: EDIT memory/projects/mr-cost-watch — extend the existing python usage parser (the price_log heredoc, lines 16-43) and the poll loop (from line ~60); writes NEW /tmp/mr_ctx_<slice>.json
steps.change: Add a `ctx` mode reusing the existing per-line JSON parse: for events where type==assistant AND parent_tool_use_id is null, compute ctx = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens; track max, last, and parent turn count; separately total the same for subagent turns. The watch loop writes /tmp/mr_ctx_<slice>.json each poll: {parent_max, parent_last, parent_turns, subagent_tokens, subagent_turns, ts}. It takes NO action and writes NO flag. Append one line per poll to $MEM/mr-native-tick.log: `<utc> CTXWATCH <slice> parent_max=<n> parent_last=<n> turns=<n>`. This is deliberately the audit-first / Gatekeeper-dryrun posture from the research: record the gauge for a full period before anything acts on it, and it repairs RF-1 at its source by storing a number instead of a bit.
steps.verification: FALSIFICATION: after one slice, /tmp/mr_ctx_<slice>.json parent_max must match an offline recomputation from /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log within 1%. Reference values MEASURED today: 13r-e parent_max 464,970 / 351 turns; 14r-g 365,476 / 266; 13r-c 191,849 / 133. If the live figure diverges, the parser is wrong and S5/S6 MUST NOT proceed — every downstream threshold depends on this number being right.
steps.risk: Low, and deliberately so. mr-cost-watch is a detached, zero-token, non-git watcher with its own lock (/tmp/mr_costwatch_<slice>.lock.d) and a documented never-touch-git contract. A parse bug produces a wrong number in a log file and nothing else, because nothing consumes it yet. Reuses the identical read path already proven by price_log.
steps.rollback: Revert the file. It is a single standalone script and no other component reads /tmp/mr_ctx_*.json at this step.

steps.title: Arm the cooperative segment cordon: threshold flag + one brief line
steps.files: EDIT memory/projects/mr-cost-watch (threshold + flag write); EDIT memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md line 13 (the existing Checkpoint + cooperative stop paragraph); EDIT memory/projects/mr-budget-config.json (new key `segment_ctx_threshold`, initial value 250000)
steps.change: mr-cost-watch: when parent_max crosses segment_ctx_threshold, write /tmp/mr_seg_<slice> once (idempotent, never re-armed within a segment) containing `ctx=<n> armed=<utc>`. Brief line 13 currently names /tmp/mr_stop_<SLICE> and /tmp/mr_stop_all at every phase boundary; extend that same existing sentence with the new flag and its DIFFERENT semantics: `/tmp/mr_seg_<SLICE>` = context-budget segment boundary — do NOT treat it as a park: finish the current phase, commit + push the wip: checkpoint, write memory/projects/monster-realm-<SLICE>-progress.md (DONE / REMAINING / BLOCKERS / exact-next-step), then exit cleanly; you WILL be relaunched to continue this same slice. Threshold 250,000 chosen from measurement: parent p50 is 200,100 so it fires only in the long tail (1,026 of 3,611 turns exceed it), and 300,000 would fire on only 509 turns (3.1% counterfactual) while 200,000 would fire on 1,810 (mid-phase risk).
steps.verification: FALSIFICATION: the flag must appear in exactly the slices whose parent context exceeds 250K and never in the others. Against today's 14 logs that predicts a flag on 13r-a(292K), 13r-b — no (241K), 13r-d(332K), 13r-e(465K), 13r-f(296K), 13r-g(368K), 13r-h(276K), 14r-a(284K), 14r-b(349K), 14r-d(295K), 14r-e(335K), 14r-g(365K) = 11 of 14; and NOT on 13r-c(192K) or 14r-c(248K). A flag on 13r-c would prove the gauge or the threshold is wrong. Second condition, and this is the one that matters: the resulting exit must be a clean checkpoint with a pushed branch and a progress memo — the same terminal shape the cost-cap wrap already produces. A segment exit that leaves an unpushed branch is a hard revert.
steps.risk: MEDIUM and this is the step that carries the real risk. If the session treats /tmp/mr_seg_ as a park it will stop the slice entirely rather than continue — which is why the flag name is distinct, the semantics are spelled out inline, and S6 (the relaunch consumer) must ship in the SAME slice. Mitigation: the checkpoint behaviour being asked for is byte-for-byte what the brief already mandates at phase boundaries and what mr-launch.sh:138 already proves works.
steps.rollback: Set segment_ctx_threshold to 0 (or delete the key) — the flag is never written and the brief line becomes inert prose. No code revert needed; this is a config-level kill switch by design.
steps.depends_on: S4 (the gauge must be verified accurate before any threshold acts on it)

steps.title: Fresh-segment relaunch loop in mr-launch.sh (must ship WITH S5)
steps.files: EDIT memory/projects/mr-launch.sh — new loop between the attempt loop (ends line 128) and the cost-cap wrap (line 130); reuses B=/tmp/mr_pass_$S.md and the PROJDIR invocation form at line 85
steps.change: After the attempt loop, while /tmp/mr_seg_$S exists AND RC==0 AND NOT terminal_pr_open AND segment count < MR_MAX_SEGMENTS (default 3) AND no stop-flag: rm the segment flag; rebuild the brief with RESUME_BLOCK populated by mr-spawn's existing template substitution, pointing at $HARNESS/projects/monster-realm/memory/projects/monster-realm-$S-progress.md and stating 'this is segment N of a context-budget split — continue the same slice from the memo; the slice scope, touches: set and ADR number are UNCHANGED'; then invoke `claude` FRESH (the line-85 form, NO --resume, same model, same effort) and re-arm the watcher. Echo `SEGMENT=N ctx_at_cut=<n>` to $L. CRITICAL: this must NOT use --resume, which restores the transcript and therefore resets nothing. Cap at 3 because the measured marginal return collapses — 2 segments give -47.6% of parent volume, 3 give -54.3%, so a 3rd buys only 6.7 points for another park-risk exposure.
steps.verification: FALSIFICATION, and it is a clean one because the counterfactual is measured per-session. For the next 5 slices compare actual parent prompt volume against that session's own unsegmented model. Predicted: -30% to -38% of parent volume (ideal -47.6% minus the MEASURED 12.1% pre-first-edit re-orientation). REFUTED, and revert, if any of: (a) parent volume falls less than 15%; (b) the segment-2 first-edit turn exceeds the segment-1 first-edit turn (baseline median ~59) — that would prove the progress memo is not carrying state and re-orientation is eating the gain; (c) any slice parks or re-derives scope after a segment cut. Condition (c) is an absolute veto regardless of the token result: the zero-scope-re-derivation property is not tradeable.
steps.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — the highest-risk step in the plan. Named hazards with mitigations: (i) a segment boundary landing mid-gauntlet — mitigated because the session, not the watcher, chooses the cut point at its next declared phase boundary; (ii) an infinite relaunch loop — mitigated by MR_MAX_SEGMENTS and by requiring RC==0; (iii) `--resume` not actually preserving context, which would make the whole design pointless — this is INFERRED from 14r-e reaching 334K across multiple attempts instead of resetting per attempt, and MUST be confirmed by a cheap probe before this step is written; (iv) the run_id/lock and the ATTEMPT/segment accounting diverging — the existing per-run lock and .done contract (`EXIT=<rc> ATTEMPTS=<n>`) must gain a SEGMENTS field so the supervisor's triage is not confused by a slice that legitimately ran 3 sessions.
steps.rollback: Set MR_MAX_SEGMENTS=0, or set segment_ctx_threshold to 0 in mr-budget-config.json (S5's kill switch disarms this step too, since the flag is never written). Both are config-only and take effect at the next launch.
steps.depends_on: S5 — and S5+S6 MUST BE ONE SLICE. They cannot be split safely in either direction: a flag with no consumer strands a checkpointed session that was promised a relaunch and never gets one (worse than the status quo, and a direct D1 violation); a consumer with no flag is dead code. This is the single step in the plan that is atomic by construction.

Hard veto: any slice merging with a weakened proof-of-teeth fixture reverts this immediately.

This step only changes what the tester is GIVEN, never whether it runs, how long it may run, or which model it uses. Reviewer, red-team and verifier (45.1% of subagent volume, the protected gauntlet) are not touched at all.

antipatterns_avoided: DO-NOT-RETRY #8 — API-level context-management beta flags (clear_thinking_20251015 / context-management-2025-06-27). Not proposed. I did find that the CLI ships `--autocompact <auto|tokens>` natively, which is a different mechanism at the correct layer, and I evaluated it seriously as approach B rather than ignoring it — then rejected it on measured grounds (6.9% upper bound, and it summarises the brief).

DO-NOT-RETRY #1 — costwatch_enforce as a KILL. The segment flag is a purely COOPERATIVE stop: the session finishes its current phase, commits, pushes, writes the memo and exits clean, then is relaunched. Nothing is killed, no lock is stranded, and the slice continues rather than being reallocated. This is the one enforcement shape the list explicitly permits.

DO-NOT-RETRY #2 — trimming the supervisor prompt to save tokens. mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md is not touched at all. S2 and S3 are justified on determinism and navigation quality; I explicitly measured and then REPORTED that the MCP token saving is only ~2.2% rather than letting an unmeasured token claim carry the argument.

DO-NOT-RETRY #3 — raising duty cycle, N_MAX or cron frequency. Nothing here changes concurrency, cadence or throughput. Segmentation changes the SHAPE of one session's context, not how many sessions run.

DO-NOT-RETRY #9 — first_repo_edit_turn as a target. I measured it (12.1% of parent volume, median turn ~59) and use it strictly as a DIAGNOSTIC in S6's refutation condition (b) — 'segment 2 must not orient slower than segment 1'. It is never a goal to minimise, precisely because minimising it would pressure against the pre-code gauntlet.

DO-NOT-RETRY #10 and #11 — tokens-per-line-added, and remediation share of spend. Every verification here is either an absolute token/turn count against a measured baseline or a binary correctness assertion. Nothing improves when the loop emits more lines.

Shortening the brief. The TARGET_DESC construction, EARS criteria, proof-of-teeth fixture, touches: block and valid-stopping-points list are byte-identical after this plan. Total addition: two single lines (S1, S3) plus one clause inside two existing sentences (S5, S7) — each with its own refutation condition so a line that does not earn its ~500x multiplier gets deleted rather than kept.

Cutting the pre-code gauntlet. Reviewer + red-team + verifier are 45.1% of subagent prompt volume and are untouched. Approach D was rejected as a headline strategy specifically because any general subagent-cost programme lands on them; only tester INPUT scoping survives, and even there the lens stays mandatory at its current model tier (D3).
Model or effort demotion under pressure (D3). No step changes --model or --effort anywhere. The segment relaunch deliberately reuses the same model and effort as the segment it continues.

Compaction of the brief. The strongest naive version of this design — just turn on --autocompact — would have quietly put the zero-scope-re-derivation property at risk. C re-sends the brief verbatim at every segment instead.

Using --resume for segmentation. This is the trap a naive reading of 'reuse machinery mr-launch.sh already has' walks straight into: mr-launch.sh:124 has a --resume path, but --resume restores the transcript and therefore resets no context at all. S6 explicitly requires a FRESH invocation and flags the --resume semantics as INFERRED with a cheap pre-implementation probe.

Acting on an unverified gauge. S4 ships in MONITOR-only mode with no consumer, mirroring the Gatekeeper dryrun / audit-first pattern from the research and the <10% effective-false-positive discipline. S5 and S6 are blocked until the live gauge matches offline recomputation within 1%.

Asserting a cause I had not verified. The workstream flagged the codegraph MCP-scope question as open; I checked it three independent ways (~/.claude.json user-scope registration, .claude/settings.json:15 pre-approval, and the live system/init event showing status 'connected') and report the stated cause as REFUTED, along with the real finding that Grep/Glob are ToolSearch-deferred — rather than building on the assumed diagnosis.

Letting a favoured hypothesis survive contact with data. My initial 'consumer MCP servers are crowding the preamble' theory predicted a ~15K-token win. A live A/B probe measured 3,105 tokens. I report the refutation in the alternatives and re-sized the step from headline to hygiene instead of quietly keeping the larger number.
